## cloudflare-containers

# Container MCP Agent

The Container MCP Agent provides access to a sandboxed container environment. This is an ephemeral container and has access to the internet.

The container is an Ubuntu 20.04 base image with the following packages installed:
- curl
- git
- net-tools
- build-essential
- nodejs
- npm
- python3
- python3-pip

If necessary, you may install additional packages.

You are given a working directory in which you can create or delete files and execute commands as described below.

If you're using python, ALWAYS use `python3` instead of `python`. ALWAYS make sure to install dependencies, as they won't be installed ahead of time.

## Resources

The primary resource in this image is the `container_files` resource. 
This is a dynamic resource, which provides a list of files defined by `file://{filepath}`, where filepath is relative to the root working directory you are in. 

The `container_files_list` allows you to list all file resources in your working directory. Content is omitted from the response of this tool.

You can read files in the container using the `container_file_read` tool. The contents are returned as a text blob with their associated mime type if it is text, 
or a base64 encoded blob for binary files.

Directories have the special mime type `inode/directory`. If `container_file_read` is called on a directory, it returns the contents of the directory as a list of resource URIs.

AVOID manually reading or writing files using the `container_exec` tool. You should prefer the dedicated file resources and tools to interact with the filesystem as it is less error prone. 

## Tools

To manage container lifecycle, use the `container_initialize` tool. If you run into errors where you can't connect to the container, attempt to restart the container with the same `container_initialize` tool. If that doesn't work, the system is probably overloaded.

You can execute actions in the container using the `container_exec` tool. By default, stdout is returned back as a string.

## cloudflare-radar

# Cloudflare Radar MCP Server

This server provides tools powered by the Cloudflare Radar API for global Internet insights.

## Authentication

- **URL Scanner** requires an active account (use `set_active_account`)
- All other Radar data tools work without account selection

## Tool Categories

- **Entities**: Look up ASN, IP, and location details (`list_autonomous_systems`, `get_as_details`, `get_ip_details`)
- **Traffic**: HTTP and DNS trends (`get_http_data`, `get_dns_queries_data`)
- **Attacks**: Layer 3/7 DDoS attack trends (`get_l3_attack_data`, `get_l7_attack_data`)
- **Email**: Routing and security trends (`get_email_routing_data`, `get_email_security_data`)
- **Quality**: Internet speed and quality metrics (`get_internet_quality_data`, `get_internet_speed_data`)
- **Rankings**: Top domains and services (`get_domains_ranking`, `get_internet_services_ranking`)
- **AI**: AI bot traffic and Workers AI usage (`get_ai_data`)
- **BGP**: Route hijacks, leaks, and stats (`get_bgp_hijacks`, `get_bgp_leaks`, `get_bgp_route_stats`)
- **Bots**: Bot traffic by category, operator, kind (`get_bots_data`)
- **Certificate Transparency**: SSL/TLS certificate issuance trends (`get_certificate_transparency_data`)
- **NetFlows**: Network traffic patterns with ADM1 filtering (`get_netflows_data`)
- **Cloud Observatory**: Cloud provider performance - AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI (`list_origins`, `get_origin_details`, `get_origins_data`)
- **URL Scanner**: Scan and analyze URLs for security threats (`search_url_scans`, `create_url_scan`, `get_url_scan`, `get_url_scan_screenshot`, `get_url_scan_har`)

## Making Comparisons

Many tools support **array-based filters** for comparisons. Filter arrays (location, asn, continent, geoId) map **positionally** to dateRange arrays - each array index corresponds to a distinct data series.

### Cross-Location Comparison (Same Time Period)
Compare HTTP traffic between Portugal and Spain over the last 7 days:
- `dateRange: ["7d", "7d"]`
- `location: ["PT", "ES"]`

## plugin:cloudflare:cloudflare-builds
# Cloudflare Workers Builds Tool
* A Cloudflare Worker is a serverless function
* Workers Builds is a CI/CD system for building and deploying your Worker whenever you push code to GitHub/GitLab.

This server allows you to view and debug Cloudflare Workers Builds for your Workers (NOT Cloudflare Pages).

To get started, you can list your accounts (accounts_list) and then set an active account (set_active_account).
Once you have an active account, you can list your Workers (workers_list) and set an active Worker (workers_builds_set_active_worker).
You can then list the builds for your Worker (workers_builds_list_builds) and set an active build (workers_builds_set_active_build).
Once you have an active build, you can view the logs (workers_builds_get_build_logs).

## Data-Catalog-App Exploration Summary

I've thoroughly explored the data-catalog-app directory. Here's what I found:

### 1. Framework & Tech Stack
- **Framework**: **Astro 6.1.3** (latest static/hybrid site generator)
- **Hosting**: Deployed on **Cloudflare Workers** via `@astrojs/cloudflare` adapter
- **Package Manager**: **pnpm**
- **Node Version Required**: >=22.12.0
- **Environment**: TypeScript with Astro strict config

### 2. UI Components Currently Used
The app is extremely minimal, containing only basic demo components:
- **Welcome.astro** - A welcome/hero component with gradient text, logo, and call-to-action buttons
- **Layout.astro** - Basic HTML layout wrapper with minimal styling
- **Custom SVG elements** - Background blur effect, Astro logo, Discord icon

**No external UI component libraries are currently installed** (no Material-UI, Shadcn, Tailwind, etc.)

### 3. Overall Structure

```
data-catalog-app/
├── src/
│   ├── assets/           # SVG graphics (astro.svg, background.svg)
│   ├── components/       # Astro components (Welcome.astro)
│   ├── layouts/          # Page layouts (Layout.astro)
│   └── pages/            # Routes (index.astro - home page)
├── public/               # Static assets (favicons)
├── dist/                 # Built output (production)
├── .astro/               # Generated types & config
├── .wrangler/            # Cloudflare Worker build artifacts
├── astro.config.mjs      # Astro configuration
├── wrangler.jsonc        # Cloudflare Worker config
├── tsconfig.json         # TypeScript config
├── package.json          # Dependencies
└── pnpm-lock.yaml        # Lockfile
```

### 4. Key Dependencies

**Production Dependencies:**
- `astro@^6.1.3` - Web framework
- `@astrojs/cloudflare@^13.1.7` - Cloudflare adapter
- `wrangler@^4.80.0` - Cloudflare CLI tool

**Overrides:**
- `vite@^7` - Build tool override

### 5. Key Files

- **astro.config.mjs** - Minimal config with Cloudflare adapter
- **wrangler.jsonc** - Worker config with:
  - Name: "flame"
  - Observability enabled
  - Assets binding pointing to `./dist`
  - Compatibility date: 2026-04-04
- **tsconfig.json** - Extends Astro strict preset

### Current State
This is a **fresh Astro starter template** that hasn't been customized yet. It's deployed as a serverless application on Cloudflare Workers. The app is completely boilerplate with no UI framework, no styling framework, and no application logic. It's ready for development but awaits implementation of the actual data catalog functionality.

## Summary of Search Results

Kumo is Cloudflare's component library for building modern web applications, and the @cloudflare/kumo package is published to the public npm registry.

**Key Features:**

- Kumo provides accessible, design-system-compliant UI components built on Base UI, handling keyboard navigation, focus management, and ARIA attributes
- It's a UI component library that helps you build accessible, responsive web apps with React and Tailwind CSS
- The current version is v1.10.0

**Components and Blocks:**

- It offers 35+ components that work seamlessly together
- Components like Button, Input, and Dialog are core UI primitives published as NPM exports
- Blocks are higher-level compositions (like PageHeader and ResourceListPage) that are installed via the Kumo CLI

**Installation and Import:**

You can install Kumo using your preferred package manager and import components either from the main package or use granular imports for better tree-shaking. The npm package name is `@cloudflare/kumo`.

You can find the official documentation at [kumo-ui.com](https://kumo-ui.com/) and the GitHub repository at [github.com/cloudflare/kumo](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Cloudflare Kumo and its relationship with Astro and React:

## Kumo Overview

Kumo is a UI component library from Cloudflare that helps you build accessible, responsive web apps with React and Tailwind CSS. It combines the accessibility primitives of Base UI with Cloudflare's design system, offering 35+ components that work seamlessly together.

## Astro Integration

The Kumo monorepo contains a component library (Base UI + Tailwind v4), an Astro docs site, and a Figma plugin. Specifically, the documentation site uses Astro with interactive component demos in the kumo-docs-astro package.

## React Components

Kumo provides accessible, design-system-compliant UI components built on Base UI. It handles keyboard navigation, focus management, and ARIA attributes so you can build accessible applications without thinking through every detail.

Kumo includes a built-in CLI for quick component reference, which reads from ai/component-registry.json (generated from TypeScript types + demo examples).

## Installation and Usage

Components can be imported using main package imports or granular imports (recommended for tree-shaking). Important: Tailwind CSS v4 does not scan node_modules/ by default, so you must add a @source directive so Tailwind can discover the utility classes used by Kumo components.

I've found comprehensive information about Cloudflare Kumo installation with React and Tailwind setup. Here are the key details:

## Installation Basics

The @cloudflare/kumo package is published to the public npm registry with no special configuration required, and you can install Kumo using your preferred package manager. The current version is v1.10.0.

## Tailwind CSS Setup

Tailwind CSS v4 does not scan node_modules/ by default, and you must add a @source directive so Tailwind can discover the utility classes used by Kumo components. In your app.css or main.css file, add the @source directive pointing to `../node_modules/@cloudflare/kumo/dist/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}` and import the Kumo styles before the tailwindcss import.

## Component Imports

Kumo requires peer dependencies including react, react-dom, and @phosphor-icons/react, which most React projects will already have installed. You can import components from the main package or use granular imports for better tree-shaking.

## CSS Distribution Options

If your application uses Tailwind CSS, add Kumo's source files to your content configuration and import the styles. Alternatively, if your application doesn't use Tailwind CSS, you can use the standalone build which includes all compiled styles by importing it in your app entry point.

For more detailed information and examples, you can visit the official installation guide at kumo-ui.com.

# Page: Overview # Overview
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [.gitignore](.gitignore) - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) - [LICENSE](LICENSE) - [README.md](README.md)
This document provides a high-level introduction to the Kumo repository, explaining its purpose as Cloudflare's component library system and the organization of the monorepo. For detailed information about specific subsystems, see: - Core package architecture → [Core Packages](#2) - Component development patterns → [Component Development Guide](#3) - CI/CD infrastructure → [CI/CD System](#4) - Version management → [Release Management](#5) - Deployment systems → [Deployment](#6) ## What is Kumo Kumo is Cloudflare's design system and component library for building modern web applications. It provides accessible, design-system-compliant React components built on [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/), with automatic dark mode support and a semantic color token system. The repository is a `pnpm` workspace monorepo containing three primary packages: | Package | Purpose | Published Name | |---------|---------|----------------| | `packages/kumo/` | React component library | `@cloudflare/kumo` | | `packages/kumo-docs-astro/` | Documentation site | Not published | | `packages/kumo-figma/` | Figma plugin for design-code sync | `@cloudflare/kumo-figma` | The system emphasizes automated tooling to maintain consistency between code, design, and documentation through code generation, custom linting, and continuous integration. **Sources:** [README.md:1-10](), [AGENTS.md:1-27]() ## Repository Structure The monorepo follows a clear organizational pattern with packages, infrastructure, and tooling separated into distinct directories: ``` kumo/ ├── packages/ │ ├── kumo/ # Component library │ ├── kumo-docs-astro/ # Documentation site │ └── kumo-figma/ # Figma plugin ├── ci/ │ ├── reporters/ # CI report aggregation │ ├── scripts/ # Deployment and validation │ ├── utils/ # Git and GitHub utilities │ └── versioning/ # Beta and production releases ├── lint/ # Custom ESLint rules ├── .changeset/ # Version management ├── lefthook.yml # Git hook configuration └── package.json # Workspace root ``` ### Package Directory: Component Library The `packages/kumo/` directory contains the core React component library: ``` packages/kumo/ ├── src/ │ ├── components/ # UI primitives (button, dialog, input) │ ├── blocks/ # Composite components (breadcrumbs, page-header) │ ├── pages/ # Full page layouts │ ├── styles/ # CSS including kumo-binding.css │ ├── utils/ # Utilities (cn, link-provider) │ ├── command-line/ # CLI implementation │ └── index.ts # Main exports ├── ai/ │ ├── component-registry.json # Machine-readable component metadata │ └── component-registry.md # Human-readable documentation ├── scripts/ │ ├── component-registry/ # Registry code generation │ ├── color/ # Token analysis │ └── generate-primitives.ts # Base UI exports └── package.json ``` The `ai/` directory contains generated component metadata that serves as the source of truth for component APIs, consumed by AI tools, the CLI, and the Figma plugin. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:84-119](), [AGENTS.md:27-74]() ### Package Directory: Documentation Site The `packages/kumo-docs-astro/` directory contains the Astro-based documentation site: ``` packages/kumo-docs-astro/ ├── src/ │ ├── components/demos/ # Interactive component demos │ ├── pages/ # File-based routing │ └── layouts/ # Page layouts ├── dist/demo-metadata.json # Generated demo metadata └── package.json ``` Demo files in `src/components/demos/` serve dual purposes: they provide interactive examples on the documentation site and serve as the source for code examples in the component registry. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:100-105]() ### Package Directory: Figma Plugin The `packages/kumo-figma/` directory contains the Figma plugin: ``` packages/kumo-figma/ ├── src/ │ ├── generators/ # 30+ component generators │ ├── parsers/ # Tailwind → Figma conversion │ ├── code.ts # Plugin entry point │ └── manifest.json # Figma plugin manifest ├── scripts/ │ └── sync-figma-tokens.ts # CSS → Figma Variables API └── package.json ``` The plugin generates Figma components from React code and synchronizes semantic color tokens from CSS to Figma variables. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:106-112](), [AGENTS.md:46-58]() ## Monorepo Architecture The following diagram shows the relationships between the three core packages and their key outputs: **Diagram: Package Dependencies and Artifacts** ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "packages/kumo" KumoSrc["src/components/"] KumoStyles["src/styles/kumo-binding.css"] KumoScripts["scripts/component-registry/"] KumoAI["ai/component-registry.json"] KumoCLI["src/command-line/"] end subgraph "packages/kumo-docs-astro" DocsDemos["src/components/demos/"] DocsDist["dist/demo-metadata.json"] DocsPages["src/pages/"] end subgraph "packages/kumo-figma" FigmaGen["src/generators/"] FigmaSync["scripts/sync-figma-tokens.ts"] end subgraph "External Outputs" NPM["npm: @cloudflare/kumo"] FigmaNPM["npm: @cloudflare/kumo-figma"] DocsWorker["Cloudflare Worker
kumo-ui.com"] FigmaVars["Figma Variables API"] end KumoSrc --> NPM KumoStyles --> NPM KumoSrc --> KumoScripts DocsDemos --> DocsDist DocsDist --> KumoScripts KumoScripts --> KumoAI KumoAI --> KumoCLI KumoCLI --> NPM KumoAI --> FigmaGen FigmaGen --> FigmaNPM KumoStyles --> FigmaSync FigmaSync --> FigmaVars DocsDemos --> DocsPages DocsPages --> DocsWorker KumoSrc -.->|"imported by"| DocsDemos ``` The component library (`packages/kumo`) is the foundation. Demo files in the documentation site consume the components and provide code examples. The component registry generation system combines TypeScript types from components with examples from demos to produce `ai/component-registry.json`, which powers the CLI and Figma plugin. The Figma plugin also syncs semantic tokens from `kumo-binding.css` to Figma's Variables API. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:27-74](), [README.md:1-84]() ## Code Generation Pipeline Kumo uses a multi-stage code generation pipeline to maintain consistency between components, documentation, and tooling: **Diagram: Code Generation Flow** ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Source Layer" TSTypes["packages/kumo/src/
TypeScript types"] Demos["packages/kumo-docs-astro/
src/components/demos/"] CSS["packages/kumo/src/styles/
kumo-binding.css"] end subgraph "Generation Layer" DemoCodegen["codegen:demos
extractDemoMetadata"] RegCodegen["codegen:registry
buildComponentRegistry"] FigmaSync["figma:sync
syncFigmaTokens"] end subgraph "Artifact Layer" DemoJSON["kumo-docs-astro/dist/
demo-metadata.json"] RegJSON["kumo/ai/
component-registry.json"] RegMD["kumo/ai/
component-registry.md"] FigmaVars["Figma Variables"] end subgraph "Consumer Layer" CLI["npx @cloudflare/kumo"] FigmaPlugin["Figma Plugin"] AI["AI Tools"] end Demos --> DemoCodegen DemoCodegen --> DemoJSON TSTypes --> RegCodegen DemoJSON --> RegCodegen RegCodegen --> RegJSON RegCodegen --> RegMD CSS --> FigmaSync FigmaSync --> FigmaVars RegJSON --> CLI RegJSON --> FigmaPlugin RegJSON --> AI RegMD --> AI FigmaVars --> FigmaPlugin ``` The pipeline runs in three stages: 1. **Demo Codegen** (`pnpm codegen:demos`): Extracts metadata from demo files into `demo-metadata.json` 2. **Registry Codegen** (`pnpm codegen:registry`): Combines TypeScript types with demo metadata to generate `component-registry.{json,md}` 3. **Figma Sync** (`pnpm figma:sync`): Pushes semantic tokens from CSS to Figma Variables API The generated artifacts serve multiple consumers: the CLI provides quick component documentation, the Figma plugin generates components and detects drift, and AI tools use the structured metadata for code assistance. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:29-44](), [AGENTS.md:54-58]() ## Development Infrastructure The repository includes several systems that enforce design system compliance and automate development workflows: **Diagram: Development Infrastructure Components** ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Enforcement Layer" LintPlugin["lint/kumo-plugin.js"] Rule1["no-primitive-colors"] Rule2["no-tailwind-dark-variant"] Rule3["enforce-variant-standard"] Rule4["no-cross-package-imports"] LintPlugin --> Rule1 LintPlugin --> Rule2 LintPlugin --> Rule3 LintPlugin --> Rule4 end subgraph "Git Hooks Layer" Lefthook["lefthook.yml"] PrePush["pre-push hook"] ValidateCS["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] Lefthook --> PrePush PrePush --> ValidateCS end subgraph "Changeset Layer" CSFiles[".changeset/*.md"] ChangesetCLI["pnpm changeset"] ChangesetCLI --> CSFiles ValidateCS -.->|"checks"| CSFiles end subgraph "Code" Components["packages/kumo/src/components/"] Components --> Rule1 Components --> Rule2 Components --> Rule3 Components -.->|"git push"| PrePush end ``` ### Custom ESLint Rules The `lint/` directory contains custom ESLint rules that prevent common design system violations: | Rule | Purpose | Error Example | |------|---------|---------------| | `no-primitive-colors` | Blocks raw Tailwind colors | `bg-blue-500` → use `bg-kumo-brand` | | `no-tailwind-dark-variant` | Prevents manual dark mode | `dark:bg-black` → tokens handle this | | `enforce-variant-standard` | Validates variant exports | Missing `KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS` | | `no-cross-package-imports` | Blocks relative cross-package imports | `../../kumo/src/` → use `@cloudflare/kumo` | These rules are configured in [lint/kumo-plugin.js]() and run during `pnpm lint`. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:61-64](), [AGENTS.md:551-577]() ### Git Hooks with Lefthook The [lefthook.yml]() configuration defines Git hooks that enforce changeset validation before pushing. When a developer pushes changes to `packages/kumo/`, the `pre-push` hook runs [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts]() to ensure a changeset file exists targeting `@cloudflare/kumo`. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:735-762]() ## CI/CD Overview The continuous integration system is organized around a reporter pattern that aggregates results from parallel CI jobs and posts consolidated PR comments: **Diagram: CI/CD Organization** ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "CI Job Layer" TestJob["test job"] LintJob["lint job"] BuildJob["build job"] CSValidate["changeset validation"] end subgraph "Report Writers" WriteNPM["write-npm-report.ts"] WriteKumo["write-kumo-docs-report.ts"] end subgraph "Artifact Storage" ReportsDir["ci/reports/"] NPMReport["npm-release-report.json"] DocsReport["kumo-docs-preview-report.json"] end subgraph "Reporter Aggregation" PostReport["post-pr-report.ts"] ReadArt["readReportArtifacts"] BuildMD["buildMarkdownComment"] end subgraph "GitHub Integration" PRComment["PR Comment"] end TestJob -.->|"triggers"| WriteNPM LintJob -.->|"triggers"| WriteKumo WriteNPM --> NPMReport WriteKumo --> DocsReport NPMReport --> ReportsDir DocsReport --> ReportsDir ReportsDir --> ReadArt ReadArt --> PostReport PostReport --> BuildMD BuildMD --> PRComment ``` The CI system consists of: 1. **Parallel Jobs**: Run tests, linting, builds, and validation concurrently 2. **Report Writers**: Generate JSON artifacts in `ci/reports/` directory 3. **Reporter Aggregation**: [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts]() reads all artifacts and combines them 4. **PR Comments**: Posts consolidated markdown comment via GitHub API For detailed documentation of the reporter architecture, see [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:944-976]() ## Release Management Kumo uses [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) for version management with two release tracks: | Release Type | Trigger | Version Format | Purpose | |-------------|---------|----------------|---------| | Beta | PR merge | `0.1.0-beta.{hash}` | Automated preview releases | | Production | Manual | `0.1.0` | Stable releases to npm | ### Beta Releases When a PR is merged, the CI pipeline automatically: 1. Runs [ci/versioning/version-beta.sh]() to append `-beta.{commit-hash}` to the version 2. Builds the package 3. Runs [ci/versioning/publish-beta.sh]() to publish to npm with `beta` tag 4. Posts PR comment with installation instructions ### Production Releases Production releases are manually triggered and create a release branch with [ci/versioning/release-production.sh](), which: 1. Creates a `release/kumo-*` branch 2. Runs `changesets version` to apply clean version numbers 3. Publishes to npm with `latest` tag 4. Creates a PR back to `main` via [ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts]() For step-by-step guides, see [Beta Release Process](#5.1) and [Production Release Process](#5.2). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:700-809]() ## Key Commands Reference The following table summarizes the most commonly used commands for working with the Kumo repository: | Command | Purpose | |---------|---------| | `pnpm install` | Install all workspace dependencies | | `pnpm dev` | Start documentation site at localhost:4321 | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build` | Build component library | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo test` | Run component tests | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo lint` | Run custom ESLint rules | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:registry` | Generate component registry | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo new-component` | Scaffold new component | | `npx @cloudflare/kumo ls` | List all components (CLI) | | `npx @cloudflare/kumo doc Button` | Get component documentation (CLI) | | `pnpm changeset` | Create changeset for version management | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo-figma build` | Build Figma plugin | | `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo-figma figma:sync` | Sync tokens to Figma | **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:72-81](), [AGENTS.md:499-540]() ## Technology Stack The repository uses the following core technologies: | Layer | Technology | |-------|-----------| | UI Framework | React with TypeScript | | Primitive Components | Base UI (by Material UI team) | | Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 with semantic tokens | | Build Tool | Vite with library mode | | Documentation | Astro with React integration | | Testing | Vitest | | Linting | oxlint with custom rules | | Package Manager | pnpm workspaces | | CI/CD | GitHub Actions | | Deployment | Cloudflare Workers | | Version Management | Changesets | The semantic token system is defined in [packages/kumo/src/styles/kumo-binding.css]() and uses CSS `light-dark()` functions to automatically handle dark mode without requiring `dark:` variants in component code. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:123-136](), [README.md:5-26]() --- # Page: Core Packages # Core Packages
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) - [README.md](README.md)
## Purpose and Scope This document provides an overview of the three main packages in the Kumo monorepo and their relationships. Each package serves a distinct purpose while working together to form a cohesive design system infrastructure. For detailed documentation of individual packages, see: - Component library implementation: [#2.1](#2.1) - Documentation site architecture: [#2.2](#2.2) - Figma plugin details: [#2.3](#2.3) ## Package Overview The Kumo monorepo contains three published packages under the `packages/` directory: | Package | npm Name | Purpose | Build Output | |---------|----------|---------|--------------| | `packages/kumo/` | `@cloudflare/kumo` | React component library with semantic token system | ESM modules, CSS, TypeScript types, CLI | | `packages/kumo-docs-astro/` | `kumo-docs-astro` | Astro-based documentation site | Static site deployed to Cloudflare Workers | | `packages/kumo-figma/` | `@cloudflare/kumo-figma` | Figma plugin for component generation | Bundled plugin code + token sync scripts | **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:84-119](), [README.md:1-84]() ## Package Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph Kumo["packages/kumo/"] KumoSrc["src/"] KumoComponents["src/components/"] KumoStyles["src/styles/"] KumoIndex["src/index.ts"] KumoRegistry["ai/component-registry.json"] KumoCLI["src/command-line/"] KumoScripts["scripts/component-registry/"] end subgraph Docs["packages/kumo-docs-astro/"] DocsDemos["src/components/demos/"] DocsPages["src/pages/"] DocsMetadata["dist/demo-metadata.json"] end subgraph Figma["packages/kumo-figma/"] FigmaGen["src/generators/"] FigmaCode["src/code.ts"] FigmaSync["scripts/figma-sync.ts"] end KumoComponents -->|"exports"| KumoIndex KumoStyles -->|"defines tokens"| KumoComponents DocsDemos -->|"codegen:demos"| DocsMetadata DocsMetadata -->|"codegen:registry"| KumoScripts KumoComponents -->|"TypeScript types"| KumoScripts KumoScripts -->|"generates"| KumoRegistry KumoRegistry -->|"powers"| KumoCLI KumoRegistry -->|"drift detection"| FigmaGen KumoIndex -->|"consumed by"| DocsPages KumoStyles -->|"parsed by"| FigmaSync FigmaSync -.->|"pushes to"| FigmaAPI["Figma Variables API"] FigmaGen -.->|"creates"| FigmaComponents["Figma Components"] ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:84-119](), [AGENTS.md:27-44]() ## Data Flow Pipeline The following diagram illustrates how code and metadata flow between packages through the code generation system: ```mermaid graph LR subgraph Input["Source Code"] TSTypes["TypeScript Types
packages/kumo/src/components/*/"] DemoFiles["Demo Files
packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/demos/"] CSSTokens["Semantic Tokens
packages/kumo/src/styles/kumo-binding.css"] end subgraph Codegen["Code Generation"] DemoCodegen["codegen:demos
extract-demos.ts"] RegCodegen["codegen:registry
component-registry/"] FigmaCodegen["figma:sync
figma-sync.ts"] end subgraph Artifacts["Generated Artifacts"] DemoMeta["demo-metadata.json"] Registry["component-registry.json
component-registry.md"] FigmaVars["Figma Variables"] end subgraph Consumers["Consumers"] CLI["CLI Commands
npx @cloudflare/kumo"] Plugin["Figma Plugin
Drift Detection"] DocsPages["Documentation Pages"] end DemoFiles --> DemoCodegen DemoCodegen --> DemoMeta DemoMeta --> RegCodegen TSTypes --> RegCodegen RegCodegen --> Registry CSSTokens --> FigmaCodegen FigmaCodegen --> FigmaVars Registry --> CLI Registry --> Plugin DemoMeta --> DocsPages ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:27-44](), [AGENTS.md:46-59]() ## @cloudflare/kumo ### Package Identity ```json { "name": "@cloudflare/kumo", "main": "./dist/index.js", "module": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } ``` **Location:** [packages/kumo/package.json]() ### Primary Exports The component library exports are structured in [packages/kumo/src/index.ts]() and include: - **Components:** React components from [packages/kumo/src/components/]() - **Blocks:** Composite components from [packages/kumo/src/blocks/]() - **Styles:** CSS including [packages/kumo/src/styles/kumo-binding.css]() - **Utils:** Helper functions like `cn()` from [packages/kumo/src/utils/]() - **CLI:** Command-line tool from [packages/kumo/src/command-line/]() - **Primitives:** Base UI re-exports (tree-shakeable) ### Generated Artifacts The package produces AI-readable metadata through its codegen system: | Artifact | Purpose | Generator | |----------|---------|-----------| | `ai/component-registry.json` | Machine-readable component metadata | [packages/kumo/scripts/component-registry/]() | | `ai/component-registry.md` | Human-readable documentation | Same as above | These artifacts are generated by running `pnpm codegen:registry` and contain props, variants, examples, and semantic token usage for all components. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:124-130](), [AGENTS.md:138-189](), [README.md:22-50]() ## kumo-docs-astro ### Package Identity ```json { "name": "kumo-docs-astro", "type": "module" } ``` **Location:** [packages/kumo-docs-astro/package.json]() ### Structure The documentation site is organized as follows: - **Pages:** File-based routing in [packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/pages/]() - **Demos:** Interactive component examples in [packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/demos/]() - **Layouts:** Page templates in [packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/layouts/]() ### Role in Ecosystem The documentation site serves three functions: 1. **Demo Source:** Demo files in [packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/demos/]() are extracted during `codegen:demos` to generate [packages/kumo-docs-astro/dist/demo-metadata.json]() 2. **Documentation Host:** Displays component documentation and examples 3. **Tool Interface:** Hosts internal tools at `/cli`, `/colors`, and `/registry` routes ### Deployment The site is deployed to Cloudflare Workers with multiple environments: - **Generator Entry:** [packages/kumo-figma/src/code.ts]() registers all generators - **Parsers:** [packages/kumo-figma/src/parsers/]() converts Tailwind classes to Figma properties - **Output:** Figma auto-layout components with semantic token bindings The plugin includes 30+ generators for components like Button, Dialog, Tabs, Toast, etc. #### Token Synchronization Located in [packages/kumo-figma/scripts/](), the sync system: 1. A test suite in [packages/kumo-figma/src/drift-detection.test.ts]() validates that generators match the registry, ensuring design-code parity. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:46-52](), [AGENTS.md:54-59](), [AGENTS.md:106-112](), [AGENTS.md:977-1005]() ## Package Dependencies ```mermaid graph TD Kumo["@cloudflare/kumo

## Purpose and Scope This document provides technical documentation for the `@cloudflare/kumo` package, the core React component library in the Kumo monorepo. It covers the package structure, exports, component architecture patterns, styling integration, and build system. For information about developing new components, see [Component Development Guide](#3). For the component registry codegen system, see [Component Registry System](#3.1). For semantic token definitions and theming, see [Semantic Token System](#3.2). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:1-120](), [README.md:1-84]() --- ## Package Overview The `@cloudflare/kumo` package is a React component library that provides accessible, design-system-compliant UI components. It is distributed as an npm package and serves as the foundation for Cloudflare's web applications. ### Core Dependencies | Dependency | Purpose | |------------|---------| | `react` | React framework (peer dependency) | | `react-dom` | React DOM rendering (peer dependency) | | `@base-ui/react` | Accessible component primitives | | `@phosphor-icons/react` | Icon library (peer dependency) | | `clsx` | Conditional className utility | | `tailwind-merge` | Tailwind class deduplication | ### Build Tooling - **Build System:** Vite in library mode for tree-shakeable ESM exports - **TypeScript:** Strict mode with full type definitions - **CSS:** Tailwind CSS v4 with custom semantic tokens - **Testing:** Vitest with React Testing Library **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:123-129](), [README.md:15-19]() --- ## Package Structure The package follows a modular directory structure organized by component type: ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "packages/kumo/" Src["src/"] Ai["ai/"] Scripts["scripts/"] subgraph "src/" Components["components/

import "@cloudflare/kumo/styles"; ``` This is the simplest import pattern but includes all components in the bundle (tree-shaking still applies at build time). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:10-13](), [README.md:24-26]() ### Granular Imports (Tree-Shaking) Import individual components for optimal bundle size: ```tsx import { Button } from "@cloudflare/kumo/components/button"; ``` Each component has a dedicated export in `package.json` configured by [scripts/generate-primitives.ts:1-300](). **Sources:** [README.md:28-32]() ### Base UI Primitives Re-exports All Base UI primitives are re-exported for advanced composition: ```tsx import { Popover } from "@cloudflare/kumo/primitives/popover"; ``` This imports [src/styles/kumo-binding.css:1-500]() which defines all semantic color tokens using CSS custom properties and `light-dark()`. **Sources:** [README.md:25-26]() --- ## Component Architecture Patterns All Kumo components follow standardized patterns enforced by custom ESLint rules (see [Custom ESLint Rules](#3.3)). ### Standard Component Structure Each component follows this file organization: ``` components/ └── button/ ├── button.tsx # Component implementation └── index.ts # Re-exports ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:336-348]() ### Diagram: Component Implementation Pattern ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Component File (button.tsx)" Imports["Imports:

This utility combines `clsx` and `tailwind-merge`: ```tsx import { cn } from "../../utils/cn"; ;\n}", "export function SecondaryButtonDemo() {\n return ;\n}" ], "semanticTokens": [ "bg-kumo-brand", "bg-kumo-control", "text-kumo-default", "ring-kumo-line" ] } } ``` This structure enables: - Type-safe code generation by AI agents - Quick CLI documentation lookup - Automated validation of Figma plugin generators **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:417-434](), [AGENTS.md:182-188]() --- ## CLI Implementation ```mermaid graph LR User["User Terminal"] NPX["npx @cloudflare/kumo"] subgraph "Command Router" Main["packages/kumo/src/command-line/index.ts

Description # - Props table (name, type, required, default) # - Variant descriptions # - Usage examples # - Semantic tokens used ``` ### Query with jq For programmatic access, query the JSON directly: ```bash # Get Button props jq '.components.Button.props' packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json # List Action category components jq '.search.byCategory.Action' packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json # Find components using bg-kumo-base token grep "bg-kumo-base" packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.md ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:145-180](), [AGENTS.md:34]() --- ## Component Requirements for Registry Components must follow these conventions to be correctly indexed by the registry: ### Required Exports Each component file must export: 1. **`KUMO_{COMPONENT}_VARIANTS`** - Variant configuration object 2. **`KUMO_{COMPONENT}_DEFAULT_VARIANTS`** - Default variant values Example from [packages/kumo/src/components/button/button.tsx](): ```typescript export const KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS = { variant: ["primary", "secondary", "ghost", "destructive"], size: ["xs", "sm", "base", "lg"], } as const; export const KUMO_BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS = { variant: "secondary", size: "base", } as const; ``` ### Optional Exports - **`KUMO_{COMPONENT}_BASE_STYLES`** - Base CSS classes (must use `KUMO_` prefix) ### File Structure Convention Components must follow the directory pattern: ``` packages/kumo/src/components/{name}/{name}.tsx ``` Examples: - `button/button.tsx` → `KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS` - `clipboard-text/clipboard-text.tsx` → `KUMO_CLIPBOARD_TEXT_VARIANTS` The registry generation script automatically converts kebab-case filenames to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constant validation. ### Enforcement The `enforce-variant-standard` ESLint rule (see [Custom ESLint Rules](#3.3)) validates these requirements at lint time, ensuring components follow the standard. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:405-467](), [AGENTS.md:560-647]() --- ## Regenerating the Registry ### When to Regenerate The registry must be regenerated after: - Adding a new component - Modifying component props or types - Adding or updating variant configurations - Updating demo files - Changing `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` exports ### Regeneration Commands ```bash # Regenerate demo metadata only pnpm --filter kumo-docs-astro codegen:demos # Regenerate component registry only pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:registry # Regenerate all codegen artifacts pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen ``` The `codegen` command runs both primitives generation and registry generation. For details on primitives generation, see [packages/kumo/scripts/generate-primitives.ts](). ### Build Integration The registry generation is integrated into the build process: ```bash # Full build includes registry generation pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build ``` This ensures the registry stays synchronized with component implementations during development and CI builds. ### Validation After regenerating, verify the changes: ```bash # Check the JSON structure jq '.components | keys' packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json # View the markdown output cat packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.md | head -50 # Test the CLI npx @cloudflare/kumo ls ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:18](), [AGENTS.md:74-77](), [AGENTS.md:486-489]() --- ## Integration with Figma Plugin The registry serves as the source of truth for Figma plugin drift detection: ### Drift Detection Test The Figma plugin includes [packages/kumo-figma/src/drift-detection.test.ts]() which validates that component generators match the registry: 1. Reads `component-registry.json` 2. Compares available component generators 3. Checks that generator configurations align with component props and variants 4. Fails if generators are missing or misaligned ### Excluded Components Some components are excluded from drift detection by adding them to the `EXCLUDED_COMPONENTS` array in the test file. This is appropriate for: - Components that cannot be represented in Figma - Complex interactive components - Components under development ### CI Enforcement The drift detection test runs in CI for pull requests that modify: - [packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.json]() - [packages/kumo-figma/src/generators/]() This prevents design-code drift by ensuring Figma plugin generators stay synchronized with component implementations. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:995-1005]() --- ## Registry as AI Interface The registry is specifically designed for AI agent consumption: ### Machine-Readable Format The JSON structure provides: - Strongly-typed prop definitions - Enumerated variant values with descriptions - Real code examples from demos - Token usage analysis This enables AI agents to: - Generate valid component usage code - Understand variant semantics - Reference correct semantic tokens - Query component capabilities programmatically ### Human-Readable Format The markdown file [packages/kumo/ai/component-registry.md]() provides: - Organized component listings - Searchable token reference - Copy-pasteable examples - Full API documentation Both formats are generated from the same source data, ensuring consistency between machine and human interfaces. ### Example AI Query Pattern ```bash # Get all components that use a specific token jq '.components | to_entries | map(select(.value.semanticTokens | contains(["bg-kumo-base"]))) | map(.key)' component-registry.json # Get required props for a component jq '.components.Dialog.props | to_entries | map(select(.value.required == true)) | map(.key)' component-registry.json ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:3](), [AGENTS.md:29-35](), [AGENTS.md:138-143]() --- ## Best Practices ### For Component Authors 1. **Always export variants** - Include `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` and `KUMO_*_DEFAULT_VARIANTS` 2. **Write JSDoc comments** - Descriptions are extracted into the registry 3. **Create demo files** - Examples are the most valuable documentation 4. **Use semantic tokens** - Token usage is tracked and displayed 5. **Regenerate after changes** - Run `codegen:registry` before committing ### For Registry Consumers 1. **Query before assuming** - Always check the registry for current component APIs 2. **Use the CLI for quick reference** - `npx @cloudflare/kumo doc Button` 3. **Parse JSON programmatically** - Use `jq` or JSON parsers for automation 4. **Check semantic tokens** - Reference the token list to ensure valid usage 5. **Read examples** - Demo code shows real-world usage patterns ### For AI Agents 1. **Never guess component APIs** - Always query the registry first 2. **Use the search index** - `search.byName` and `search.byCategory` provide fast lookups 3. **Respect variant defaults** - Use `props[].default` for optional props 4. **Reference examples** - Copy patterns from `examples[]` array 5. **Validate tokens** - Only use tokens listed in `semanticTokens[]` or `kumoColors[]` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:899-928]() --- ## Troubleshooting ### Registry Generation Fails **Problem:** `codegen:registry` fails with TypeScript errors **Solution:** 1. Ensure all component files follow the `{name}/{name}.tsx` pattern 2. Check that TypeScript compiles: `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo typecheck` 3. Verify `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` exports match the component name 4. Run the custom lint rule: `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo lint` ### Demo Metadata Missing **Problem:** Registry shows no examples for a component **Solution:** 1. Check demo file exists: `packages/kumo-docs-astro/src/components/demos/{Name}Demo.tsx` 2. Regenerate demo metadata: `pnpm --filter kumo-docs-astro codegen:demos` 3. Verify demo exports are named correctly 4. Ensure demo file extension is `.tsx` (not `.ts`) ### CLI Command Not Found **Problem:** `npx @cloudflare/kumo` fails with "command not found" **Solution:** 1. Ensure package is built: `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build` 2. Check `bin` field in `package.json` points to built CLI file 3. Verify `component-registry.json` exists in `packages/kumo/ai/` 4. Try clearing npm cache: `npx clear-npx-cache` ### Stale Registry Data **Problem:** Registry shows outdated component information **Solution:** 1. Regenerate registry: `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo codegen:registry` 2. Check if changes were made to `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` exports 3. Verify TypeScript types changed in component files 4. Clear build cache: `rm -rf packages/kumo/dist` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:486-489](), [AGENTS.md:899-942]() --- # Page: Semantic Token System # Semantic Token System

## Purpose and Scope The Semantic Token System provides a design-system-level abstraction over raw CSS colors through CSS custom properties. This system ensures consistent theming, automatic light/dark mode support, and design-code synchronization. All Kumo components use semantic tokens exclusively, never raw Tailwind colors. This document covers token definitions, the light-dark mode mechanism, theming capabilities, and enforcement patterns. For information about specific component styling patterns, see [Component Development Guide](#3). For custom lint rules that enforce token usage, see [Custom ESLint Rules](#3.3). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:1-256]() --- ## System Architecture The semantic token system operates across multiple layers: CSS definitions, component consumption, lint enforcement, and design synchronization. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Definition Layer" KumoCSS["kumo-binding.css
CSS Custom Properties"] LightDark["light-dark() Function
Mode-aware values"] end subgraph "Application Layer" DataMode["data-mode attribute
'light' | 'dark'"] DataTheme["data-theme attribute
'fedramp' | custom"] ColorScheme["color-scheme property
Browser integration"] end subgraph "Component Layer" TailwindClasses["Tailwind Classes
bg-kumo-base
text-kumo-default
border-kumo-line"] Components["React Components
Button, Dialog, Input, etc."] end subgraph "Enforcement Layer" NoPrimitiveColors["no-primitive-colors
ESLint rule"] NoDarkVariant["no-tailwind-dark-variant
ESLint rule"] end subgraph "Design Sync Layer" FigmaSync["figma:sync script
CSS → Figma Variables API"] FigmaVars["Figma Variables
Design token parity"] end KumoCSS --> LightDark LightDark --> TailwindClasses DataMode --> ColorScheme ColorScheme --> LightDark DataTheme --> KumoCSS TailwindClasses --> Components Components --> NoPrimitiveColors Components --> NoDarkVariant KumoCSS --> FigmaSync FigmaSync --> FigmaVars style KumoCSS fill:#f9f9f9 style Components fill:#f9f9f9 style FigmaSync fill:#f9f9f9 ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:206-334]() --- ## Token Definition System ### CSS Custom Properties All semantic tokens are defined as CSS custom properties in `packages/kumo/src/styles/kumo-binding.css` using the `light-dark()` function. This function accepts two values: the first for light mode, the second for dark mode. ```css @layer base { :root { --color-surface: light-dark(#ffffff, #1a1a1a); --color-active: light-dark(#0052cc, #4c9aff); --text-color-default: light-dark(#172b4d, #ffffff); } } ``` The `color-scheme` property controls which value `light-dark()` resolves to: ```css :root { color-scheme: light; } [data-mode="dark"] { color-scheme: dark; } ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:206-295]() ### Tailwind Integration Semantic tokens are exposed as Tailwind utility classes through CSS custom properties. The naming convention follows: `{property}-kumo-{semantic-name}`. | CSS Custom Property | Tailwind Class | Usage | |---------------------|----------------|-------| | `--color-surface` | `bg-kumo-base` | Base background surfaces | | `--text-color-default` | `text-kumo-default` | Default text color | | `--color-line` | `border-kumo-line` | Border colors | | `--color-ring` | `ring-kumo-ring` | Focus ring colors | | `--color-brand` | `bg-kumo-brand` | Brand/primary colors | **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:208-242]() --- ## Light/Dark Mode Mechanism ### Mode Attribute System The `data-mode` attribute controls the color scheme resolution. Set this attribute on a parent element, typically `` or ``. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Mode Control" HTML[""] HTMLDark[""] end subgraph "CSS Resolution" ColorScheme["color-scheme property

// ✅ CORRECT - Automatic dark mode via semantic tokens
``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:242-256](), [AGENTS.md:267-295]() --- ## Theme System ### Theme Attribute The `data-theme` attribute enables theme-specific token overrides. Themes are defined in `kumo-binding.css` within the `@layer base` directive. ```css @layer base { [data-theme="fedramp"] { --color-surface: light-dark(#f5f5f5, #262626); --color-active: light-dark(#1a73e8, #8ab4f8); --text-color-surface: light-dark(#202124, #e8eaed); } } ``` ### Existing Themes | Theme | Attribute Value | Purpose | |-------|----------------|---------| | Default | (none) | Standard Cloudflare branding | | FedRAMP | `data-theme="fedramp"` | Government compliance styling | ### Creating Custom Themes 1. **Define theme overrides in kumo-binding.css:** ```css @layer base { [data-theme="custom-theme"] { --color-surface: light-dark(#custom-light, #custom-dark); --color-active: light-dark(#custom-light, #custom-dark); --text-color-surface: light-dark(#custom-light, #custom-dark); } } ``` 2. **Apply the theme attribute:** ```tsx
{/* All Kumo components use theme overrides */}
``` ### Theme Guidelines - **Use `light-dark()` for all token overrides:** Ensures themes work in both light and dark modes - **Override sparingly:** Only override tokens that need to change - **Target semantic tokens only:** Override `--color-*` and `--text-color-*` variables, not component-specific styles - **Test both modes:** Verify theme appearance in both light and dark mode **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:296-334]() --- ## Token Categories Semantic tokens are organized into functional categories based on their usage patterns. The complete token reference is available in the component registry. ### Surface Tokens Control background colors for different elevation levels. | Token | Class | Purpose | Hierarchy | Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) - [lint/kumo-plugin.js](lint/kumo-plugin.js) - [lint/no-cross-package-imports.js](lint/no-cross-package-imports.js)
This document describes the custom ESLint rules implemented in the Kumo repository to enforce design system compliance. These rules prevent common mistakes when building components, such as using raw Tailwind colors instead of semantic tokens, manually handling dark mode, or violating component naming conventions. For information about the semantic token system that these rules enforce, see [Semantic Token System](#3.2). For general development tool configuration, see [Development Tools](#7). ## Purpose and Scope The custom ESLint rules in Kumo serve as automated gatekeepers for design system compliance. They catch violations at development time, ensuring that: - All components use semantic tokens (e.g., `bg-kumo-base`) instead of raw Tailwind colors (e.g., `bg-blue-500`) - Dark mode is handled automatically through semantic tokens, not manual `dark:` variants - Components follow the `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` naming convention for variant exports - Packages import from each other using proper package names, not relative paths These rules run as part of the standard lint command and are enforced in CI pipelines before code can be merged. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:60-83](), [lint/kumo-plugin.js:1-19]() ## Plugin Architecture The custom rules are organized as an ESLint plugin named `kumo`, defined in `lint/kumo-plugin.js`. The plugin exports a meta object and a rules registry that maps rule names to their implementations. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Plugin Definition" Plugin["kumo-plugin.js

Each rule exports a `defineRule` call that returns a rule object with: - `meta`: Rule metadata including type, documentation, error messages, and schema - `defaultOptions`: Default configuration options - `createOnce`: Factory function that returns AST visitor methods **Sources:** [lint/kumo-plugin.js:1-19]() ## Rule Reference ### no-primitive-colors **Purpose:** Prevents use of raw Tailwind color utilities and enforces semantic token usage. **Rationale:** Raw Tailwind colors (e.g., `bg-blue-500`, `text-gray-900`) break theming and dark mode support. All styling must use semantic tokens (e.g., `bg-kumo-base`, `text-kumo-default`) defined in `packages/kumo/src/styles/kumo-binding.css`. **Implementation:** The rule validates Tailwind class names in JSX `className` attributes and template strings. It checks against a list of primitive color patterns and validates that semantic tokens exist in the theme CSS file. **Violations:** | ❌ Invalid | ✅ Valid | |-----------|---------| | `className="bg-blue-500"` | `className="bg-kumo-brand"` | | `className="text-gray-900"` | `className="text-kumo-default"` | | `className="border-red-600"` | `className="border-kumo-danger"` | | `className="ring-indigo-500"` | `className="ring-kumo-ring"` | **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:552-555](), [AGENTS.md:62]() ### no-tailwind-dark-variant **Purpose:** Disallows use of Tailwind's `dark:` variant prefix in class names. **Rationale:** Kumo's semantic token system automatically handles dark mode through CSS `light-dark()` functions. Manual dark mode handling with `dark:` creates maintenance burden and can conflict with the automatic system. **Implementation:** The rule scans all `className` attributes and template strings for the `dark:` prefix pattern. **Violations:** | ❌ Invalid | ✅ Valid | |-----------|---------| | `className="bg-white dark:bg-black"` | `className="bg-kumo-base"` | | `className="text-black dark:text-white"` | `className="text-kumo-default"` | | `className="dark:opacity-50"` | `className="opacity-50"` (with token handling light/dark) | **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:557-559](), [AGENTS.md:63](), [AGENTS.md:243-255]() ### enforce-variant-standard **Purpose:** Enforces the `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` and `KUMO_*_DEFAULT_VARIANTS` naming convention for component exports. **Rationale:** Component variant configuration must be exported in a standardized format for the component registry system to extract metadata. This enables the CLI tools and Figma plugin to understand component APIs. **Scope:** Only applies to files matching the pattern `src/components/{name}/{name}.tsx`. **Implementation:** The rule extracts the component name from the file path, converts it to `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, and validates that the file exports: - `KUMO_{COMPONENT}_VARIANTS` (required) - `KUMO_{COMPONENT}_DEFAULT_VARIANTS` (required) - `KUMO_{COMPONENT}_BASE_STYLES` (optional, but must have `KUMO_` prefix if present) ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "File Path Processing" Path["src/components/button/button.tsx"] Extract["Extract: 'button'"] Transform["Transform: 'BUTTON'"] end subgraph "Required Exports" V1["KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS"] V2["KUMO_BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS"] end subgraph "Optional Exports" V3["KUMO_BUTTON_BASE_STYLES"] end Path --> Extract Extract --> Transform Transform -->|validates| V1 Transform -->|validates| V2 Transform -->|validates| V3 ``` **File Path Conversions:** | File Path | Component Name | Required Export Prefix | |-----------|----------------|----------------------| | `src/components/button/button.tsx` | `button` | `KUMO_BUTTON_` | | `src/components/clipboard-text/clipboard-text.tsx` | `clipboard-text` → `clipboard_text` | `KUMO_CLIPBOARD_TEXT_` | | `src/components/page-header/page-header.tsx` | `page-header` → `page_header` | `KUMO_PAGE_HEADER_` | **Violations:** ```tsx // ❌ WRONG - Missing KUMO_ prefix export const BUTTON_VARIANTS = { /* ... */ }; export const BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS = { /* ... */ }; // ❌ WRONG - Wrong component name (in button.tsx) export const KUMO_INPUT_VARIANTS = { /* ... */ }; export const KUMO_INPUT_DEFAULT_VARIANTS = { /* ... */ }; // ❌ WRONG - Missing required DEFAULT_VARIANTS export const KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS = { /* ... */ }; // Error: Component must export KUMO_BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS // ❌ WRONG - BASE_STYLES without KUMO_ prefix export const BUTTON_BASE_STYLES = "..."; // ✅ CORRECT - Valid exports in button.tsx export const KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS = { variant: ["primary", "secondary", "ghost", "destructive"], size: ["xs", "sm", "base", "lg"], }; export const KUMO_BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS = { variant: "secondary", size: "base", }; export const KUMO_BUTTON_BASE_STYLES = "flex items-center font-medium"; ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:561-647]() ### no-cross-package-imports **Purpose:** Prevents relative imports that traverse into sibling packages in the monorepo. **Rationale:** Packages should import from each other using their published package names (e.g., `@cloudflare/kumo`), not relative paths. Relative imports break encapsulation, bypass proper exports, and create tight coupling between packages. **Detection Logic:** The rule identifies cross-package imports by: 1. Checking if the import path starts with `../` (going up from current directory) 2. Counting the number of `../` sequences to determine if it escapes the package boundary 3. Checking if the target directory matches a known package name (`kumo`, `kumo-docs-astro`, `kumo-figma`) 4. Requiring at least 2 levels of traversal (`../../`) to avoid false positives for local directories **Implementation Details:** [lint/no-cross-package-imports.js:1-164]() The `getCrossPackageImport` function analyzes import paths: ```mermaid graph TB Start["Import Path Analysis"] Check1{"Starts with '../'?"} Check2{"Matches Pattern

Violations block pull request merges. The CI configuration includes these lint jobs: - Standard oxlint execution across all packages - Type-aware linting with TypeScript configuration - Custom rule validation on component files **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:945-957]() ### Git Hook Integration While changesets are validated in pre-push hooks (see [Git Hooks with Lefthook](#7.1)), the linter runs independently. Developers should run linting locally before committing to catch violations early. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:738-762]() ## Relationship to Component Registry The `enforce-variant-standard` rule directly supports the component registry system (see [Component Registry System](#3.1)). By ensuring components export `KUMO_*_VARIANTS` and `KUMO_*_DEFAULT_VARIANTS` in a standardized format, the codegen system can reliably extract variant metadata. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Component Development" Component["button.tsx"] Exports["KUMO_BUTTON_VARIANTS
KUMO_BUTTON_DEFAULT_VARIANTS"] end subgraph "Lint Enforcement" Rule["enforce-variant-standard"] Validate["Validate naming
Validate presence"] end subgraph "Registry Generation" Codegen["codegen:registry"] Registry["component-registry.json"] end subgraph "Consumers" CLI["npx @cloudflare/kumo doc"] Figma["Figma Plugin"] end Component --> Exports Exports -->|checked by| Rule Rule --> Validate Validate -->|ensures correct format| Codegen Codegen -->|extracts| Exports Codegen --> Registry Registry --> CLI Registry --> Figma ``` Without this rule, the registry codegen system would fail or produce incorrect metadata, breaking the CLI and Figma plugin. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:561-647](), [AGENTS.md:29-44]() ## Configuration Example The custom rules are configured in the ESLint configuration file at the workspace root. A typical configuration looks like: ```json { "plugins": ["kumo"], "rules": { "kumo/no-primitive-colors": "error", "kumo/no-tailwind-dark-variant": "error", "kumo/enforce-variant-standard": "error", "kumo/no-cross-package-imports": "error" } } ``` All rules are configured as `"error"` to block CI pipelines and prevent violations from being merged. **Sources:** [lint/kumo-plugin.js:1-19]() ## Error Message Reference Each rule provides descriptive error messages with actionable guidance: | Rule | Message Format | |------|----------------| | `no-primitive-colors` | Identifies the specific primitive color class and suggests using semantic tokens | | `no-tailwind-dark-variant` | Points to the `dark:` usage and explains that semantic tokens handle dark mode automatically | | `enforce-variant-standard` | Lists missing or incorrectly named exports with the expected format | | `no-cross-package-imports` | Shows the problematic import path and suggests the correct package import | **Sources:** [lint/kumo-plugin.js:1-19](), [lint/no-cross-package-imports.js:86-96]() ## Summary The custom ESLint rules serve as the first line of defense for design system compliance in Kumo. They: - **Prevent theming violations** by blocking raw Tailwind colors - **Enforce automatic dark mode** by disallowing manual `dark:` variants - **Enable code generation** by standardizing variant export naming - **Maintain architectural boundaries** by preventing cross-package relative imports These rules run automatically during development, in CI pipelines, and integrate with the broader component registry ecosystem to ensure consistency across the design system. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:60-83](), [lint/kumo-plugin.js:1-19]() --- # Page: CI/CD System # CI/CD System

## Purpose and Scope The CI/CD System provides the continuous integration and deployment infrastructure for the Kumo monorepo. It implements a reporter pattern that collects results from multiple CI jobs and aggregates them into consolidated PR comments. This document covers the core reporter architecture, artifact management, and context propagation. For release-specific workflows (beta and production), see [Release Management](#5). For deployment of documentation previews and staging, see [Deployment](#6). For individual CI script implementations, see [CI Script Reference](#4.3). ## Architecture Overview The CI/CD system is built around a reporter pattern where individual CI jobs write report artifacts as JSON files, which are then collected and posted as a single PR comment. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "CI Jobs (Parallel Execution)" Job1["Job: Build @cloudflare/kumo"] Job2["Job: Deploy Docs Preview"] Job3["Job: Run Tests"] Job4["Job: Validate Changesets"] end subgraph "Artifact Generation" Job1 -->|"writeReportArtifact()"| Artifact1["ci/reports/npm-release.json"] Job2 -->|"writeReportArtifact()"| Artifact2["ci/reports/kumo-docs-preview.json"] Job3 -->|"writeReportArtifact()"| Artifact3["ci/reports/test-results.json"] end subgraph "Reporter Aggregation" Artifact1 --> ReadAll["readReportArtifacts()"] Artifact2 --> ReadAll Artifact3 --> ReadAll ReadAll --> Items["ReportItem[]"] Context["buildContextFromEnv()"] Context --> CIContext["CIContext object"] Items --> BuildMD["buildMarkdownComment()"] CIContext --> BuildMD end subgraph "PR Comment System" BuildMD --> PRComment["Consolidated PR Comment"] PRComment --> GitHub["GitHub API"] end Job4 -.->|"validates before other jobs"| Job1 ``` **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:1-144](), Diagram 2 from high-level architecture ## Reporter Pattern The reporter system is built on three core interfaces defined in [ci/reporters/types.ts:24-78](): ### ReportItem Interface A `ReportItem` represents a single section in the PR comment: | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for the report type (e.g., `"npm-release"`) | | `title` | `string` | Section title displayed in the PR comment | | `priority` | `number` | Sort order (lower appears first; 10-19 for releases, 20-29 for previews) | | `content` | `string` | Markdown content for this section | | `success` | `boolean` | Whether the operation was successful | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:24-39]() ### CIContext Interface The `CIContext` provides environment data to reporters: | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `commitSha` | `string` | Full commit SHA from `GITHUB_SHA` | | `shortSha` | `string` | First 8 characters of commit SHA | | `prNumber` | `string` | PR number from `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` or `PR_NUMBER` | | `repository` | `string` | Repository name (defaults to `"cloudflare/kumo"`) | | `apiToken` | `string` | GitHub API token from `GITHUB_TOKEN` | | `packageName` | `string` | Package name (defaults to `"@cloudflare/kumo"`) | | `packageVersion` | `string` | Package version being released | | `kumoDocsPreviewUrl` | `string?` | Documentation preview URL if deployed | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:44-63]() ### Reporter Interface Each reporter implements the `Reporter` interface: ```typescript interface Reporter { id: string; // Matches ReportItem.id name: string; // Human-readable name for logging collect(context: CIContext): Promise; } ``` The `collect()` method returns `null` if the reporter should be skipped (e.g., no deployment occurred). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:68-78]() ## Report Artifact Lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Job as "CI Job" participant WRA as "writeReportArtifact()" participant FS as "ci/reports/*.json" participant RRA as "readReportArtifacts()" participant Reporter as "Reporter.collect()" participant Agg as "Aggregation Script" participant GH as "GitHub API" Note over Job,FS: Phase 1: Job Execution Job->>WRA: Call with ReportItem WRA->>FS: Write JSON file Note over FS: Artifact stored for collection Note over FS,GH: Phase 2: Report Collection Agg->>RRA: Read all artifacts RRA->>FS: Scan ci/reports/ directory FS-->>RRA: Return all .json files RRA-->>Agg: Return ReportItem[] Note over Agg,GH: Phase 3: Additional Reporters Agg->>Reporter: collect(context) Reporter-->>Agg: Return ReportItem | null Note over Agg,GH: Phase 4: Post to GitHub Agg->>Agg: Build markdown comment Agg->>GH: Post consolidated comment ``` **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:99-143](), Diagram 2 from high-level architecture ### Phase 1: Artifact Writing Individual CI jobs call `writeReportArtifact()` to persist their results: ```typescript writeReportArtifact(item: ReportItem): void ``` This function: 1. Creates the `ci/reports` directory if it doesn't exist [ci/reporters/types.ts:103-105]() 2. Writes the item to `ci/reports/${item.id}.json` [ci/reporters/types.ts:106]() 3. Logs the file path [ci/reporters/types.ts:108]() **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:99-109]() ### Phase 2: Artifact Reading The aggregation script calls `readReportArtifacts()` to collect all reports: ```typescript interface ReadReportResult { items: ReportItem[]; failures: string[]; } ``` This function: 1. Scans the `ci/reports` directory for `.json` files [ci/reporters/types.ts:128]() 2. Parses each file into a `ReportItem` [ci/reporters/types.ts:132-135]() 3. Collects parsing failures for error handling [ci/reporters/types.ts:137]() 4. Returns both successful items and failure paths [ci/reporters/types.ts:142]() **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:114-143]() ### Phase 3: Dynamic Reporter Collection After reading artifacts, the aggregation script calls each registered reporter's `collect()` method to gather additional data that wasn't written as artifacts (e.g., querying npm registry for verification). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:68-78]() ## Context Building The `buildContextFromEnv()` function extracts CI context from GitHub Actions environment variables: | Environment Variable | Context Field | Default Value | |---------------------|---------------|---------------| | `GITHUB_SHA` | `commitSha`, `shortSha` | `""` | | `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` or `PR_NUMBER` | `prNumber` | `""` | | `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` | `repository` | `"cloudflare/kumo"` | | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `apiToken` | `""` | | `PACKAGE_NAME` | `packageName` | `"@cloudflare/kumo"` | | `PACKAGE_VERSION` | `packageVersion` | `""` | | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` | `kumoDocsPreviewUrl` | `undefined` | The `shortSha` is derived by taking the first 8 characters of `commitSha` [ci/reporters/types.ts:88](). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:84-96]() ## Reporter Registry The reporter registry in [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-29]() maintains an ordered list of all active reporters: ```mermaid graph LR Registry["reporters: Reporter[]"] NPM["npmReleaseReporter
id: 'npm-release'
priority: 10"] Docs["kumoDocsPreviewReporter
id: 'kumo-docs-preview'
priority: 20"] Registry --> NPM Registry --> Docs NPM -.->|"lower priority = first"| Docs ``` The registry array defines execution order [ci/reporters/index.ts:15-18](). Reporters are imported from individual modules [ci/reporters/index.ts:9-10]() and must implement the `Reporter` interface. To add a new reporter: 1. Implement the `Reporter` interface in a new file 2. Import the reporter in [ci/reporters/index.ts]() 3. Add it to the `reporters` array 4. Export it for use in scripts **Sources:** [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-29]() ## Directory Structure The CI/CD system uses the following directory structure: ``` ci/ ├── reports/ # Artifact storage directory │ ├── npm-release.json # Written by npm publishing jobs │ ├── kumo-docs-preview.json # Written by docs deployment jobs │ └── *.json # Additional report artifacts ├── reporters/ │ ├── types.ts # Core interfaces and utilities │ ├── index.ts # Reporter registry │ ├── npm-release.ts # npm release reporter │ └── kumo-docs-preview.ts # Docs preview reporter └── scripts/ ├── post-pr-report.ts # Main aggregation script ├── write-npm-report.ts # npm artifact writer └── write-kumo-docs-report.ts # Docs artifact writer ``` The `REPORTS_DIR` constant is defined as `"ci/reports"` [ci/reporters/types.ts:19](). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:19](), [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-29]() ## Integration Points The CI/CD system integrates with: | System | Integration Point | Purpose | |--------|------------------|---------| | GitHub Actions | Environment variables (`GITHUB_*`) | Provides context for report generation | | npm Registry | Reporter `collect()` methods | Verifies package publication | | Cloudflare Workers | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` env var | Links to deployed documentation | | Release Management | `PACKAGE_NAME`, `PACKAGE_VERSION` | Coordinates with versioning scripts (see [Release Management](#5)) | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:84-96](), Diagrams 2 and 3 from high-level architecture ##
