## Purpose and Scope The Reporter System is a CI/CD infrastructure component that aggregates results from multiple parallel CI jobs and consolidates them into a single PR comment. This system enables each CI job to independently publish structured report data as JSON artifacts, which are later collected and formatted into a unified markdown comment. This document covers the reporter architecture, core interfaces, artifact management patterns, and built-in reporter implementations. For information about how aggregated reports are posted to GitHub PRs, see [PR Comment Automation](#4.2). For documentation of individual CI scripts that generate reports, see [CI Script Reference](#4.3). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:1-7]() --- ## System Overview The Reporter System operates in two distinct phases across separate CI jobs: **Phase 1: Artifact Generation** - Individual CI jobs (e.g., beta release, docs preview) execute reporters that write `ReportItem` artifacts as JSON files to `ci/reports/`. **Phase 2: Aggregation** - A final CI job reads all artifacts from `ci/reports/`, sorts them by priority, formats them into markdown, and posts a consolidated PR comment. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Phase 1: Artifact Generation" BetaJob["CI Job: Beta Release"] DocsJob["CI Job: Docs Preview"] BetaJob --> BetaReporter["npmReleaseReporter.collect()"] DocsJob --> DocsReporter["kumoDocsPreviewReporter.collect()"] BetaReporter --> BetaItem["ReportItem
{id: 'npm-release', priority: 10}"] DocsReporter --> DocsItem["ReportItem
{id: 'kumo-docs-preview', priority: 30}"] BetaItem --> WriteArt1["writeReportArtifact()"] DocsItem --> WriteArt2["writeReportArtifact()"] WriteArt1 --> Artifact1["ci/reports/npm-release.json"] WriteArt2 --> Artifact2["ci/reports/kumo-docs-preview.json"] end subgraph "Phase 2: Aggregation" ReportJob["CI Job: Post PR Report"] Artifact1 --> ReadArt["readReportArtifacts()"] Artifact2 --> ReadArt ReadArt --> Items["ReportItem[]
sorted by priority"] Items --> Markdown["buildMarkdownComment()"] Markdown --> Post["postPRComment()"] Post --> PRComment["GitHub PR Comment"] end style Artifact1 fill:#f9f9f9 style Artifact2 fill:#f9f9f9 style PRComment fill:#f9f9f9 ``` **Diagram: Two-Phase Reporter Architecture** The artifact-based approach decouples report generation from aggregation, allowing CI jobs to complete independently without blocking each other. Each job only needs to write its own artifact; the aggregation job handles ordering and formatting. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:1-7](), [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-11]() --- ## Core Interfaces ### ReportItem The `ReportItem` interface defines the structure of a single report section. Each artifact generated by a CI job must conform to this interface. ```mermaid classDiagram class ReportItem { +string id +string title +number priority +string content +boolean success } note for ReportItem "Written to ci/reports/{id}.json" ``` **Diagram: ReportItem Interface Structure** | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for the report type (e.g., `"npm-release"`, `"kumo-docs-preview"`) | | `title` | `string` | Section title displayed in the PR comment (e.g., `"📦 NPM Package"`) | | `priority` | `number` | Sort order in the final comment. Lower numbers appear first. Range: 10-19 for releases, 20-29 for previews | | `content` | `string` | Markdown-formatted content for this section | | `success` | `boolean` | Whether this item represents a successful operation | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:21-39]() ### CIContext The `CIContext` interface provides environment data to reporters. It is constructed from GitHub Actions environment variables and contains information about the current CI run. ```mermaid classDiagram class CIContext { +string commitSha +string shortSha +string prNumber +string repository +string apiToken +string packageName +string packageVersion +string? kumoDocsPreviewUrl } class buildContextFromEnv { <> } buildContextFromEnv ..> CIContext : creates note for buildContextFromEnv "Reads from process.env.GITHUB_*" ``` **Diagram: CIContext Construction** The `buildContextFromEnv()` function constructs a `CIContext` from environment variables: | CIContext Field | Environment Variable | Fallback | |-----------------|---------------------|----------| | `commitSha` | `GITHUB_SHA` | `""` | | `shortSha` | Derived from `commitSha` | First 8 characters | | `prNumber` | `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` or `PR_NUMBER` | `""` | | `repository` | `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` | `"cloudflare/kumo"` | | `apiToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `""` | | `packageName` | `PACKAGE_NAME` | `"@cloudflare/kumo"` | | `packageVersion` | `PACKAGE_VERSION` | `""` | | `kumoDocsPreviewUrl` | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` | `undefined` | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:41-96]() ### Reporter The `Reporter` interface defines the contract for reporter implementations. Each reporter implements a `collect()` method that generates a `ReportItem` or returns `null` if the reporter should be skipped. ```mermaid classDiagram class Reporter { <> +string id +string name +collect(context: CIContext) Promise~ReportItem | null~ } class npmReleaseReporter { +id: "npm-release" +name: "NPM Release" +collect(context) } class kumoDocsPreviewReporter { +id: "kumo-docs-preview" +name: "Kumo Docs Preview" +collect(context) } Reporter <|.. npmReleaseReporter Reporter <|.. kumoDocsPreviewReporter ``` **Diagram: Reporter Interface and Implementations** The `collect()` method receives a `CIContext` and returns: - `ReportItem` - Report data to include in the PR comment - `null` - Skip this reporter (e.g., when required environment variables are missing) **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:65-78](), [ci/reporters/npm-release.ts:9-11](), [ci/reporters/kumo-docs-preview.ts:9-11]() --- ## Artifact Management ### Writing Artifacts CI jobs write report artifacts using `writeReportArtifact()`. This function creates the `ci/reports/` directory if it doesn't exist and writes the `ReportItem` as a JSON file. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Job as "CI Job" participant Reporter as "Reporter.collect()" participant Write as "writeReportArtifact()" participant FS as "File System" Job->>Reporter: Execute with CIContext Reporter->>Reporter: Generate ReportItem Reporter->>Job: Return ReportItem Job->>Write: writeReportArtifact(item) Write->>FS: Check if ci/reports/ exists alt Directory missing Write->>FS: mkdirSync("ci/reports/", recursive) end Write->>FS: writeFileSync("ci/reports/{id}.json", JSON) Write->>Job: Log confirmation ``` **Diagram: Artifact Writing Sequence** The artifact file name is derived from the `ReportItem.id` field. For example, a `ReportItem` with `id: "npm-release"` is written to `ci/reports/npm-release.json`. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:98-109]() ### Reading Artifacts The aggregation job reads all artifacts using `readReportArtifacts()`. This function scans the `ci/reports/` directory for `.json` files and parses them into `ReportItem` objects. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Job as "Aggregation Job" participant Read as "readReportArtifacts()" participant FS as "File System" Job->>Read: readReportArtifacts() Read->>FS: Check if ci/reports/ exists alt Directory missing Read->>Job: Return {items: [], failures: []} end Read->>FS: readdirSync("ci/reports/") FS->>Read: ["npm-release.json", "kumo-docs-preview.json"] Read->>Read: Filter for .json files loop For each file Read->>FS: readFileSync(file) FS->>Read: JSON content Read->>Read: JSON.parse() alt Parse success Read->>Read: Add to items[] else Parse failure Read->>Read: Add to failures[] Read->>Read: Log warning end end Read->>Job: Return {items, failures} ``` **Diagram: Artifact Reading Sequence** The function returns a `ReadReportResult` object containing: - `items: ReportItem[]` - Successfully parsed report items - `failures: string[]` - File names that failed to parse **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:111-143]() --- ## Reporter Registry The reporter registry in [ci/reporters/index.ts]() maintains an ordered list of all available reporters. This registry determines which reporters execute during artifact generation. ```mermaid graph LR Registry["reporters: Reporter[]"] --> NPM["npmReleaseReporter"] Registry --> Docs["kumoDocsPreviewReporter"] NPM -.->|priority: 10| Comment["PR Comment"] Docs -.->|priority: 30| Comment Note["Add new reporters
to this array"] Note -.-> Registry ``` **Diagram: Reporter Registry Pattern** The registry is defined as: ```typescript export const reporters: Reporter[] = [ npmReleaseReporter, kumoDocsPreviewReporter, ]; ``` Reporters are executed in the order they appear in this array during Phase 1 (artifact generation). However, the final comment order is determined by each `ReportItem.priority` field, not the registry order. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/index.ts:12-18]() --- ## Built-in Reporters ### npmReleaseReporter The `npmReleaseReporter` generates a report when a new npm package version is published. It displays the package version and installation instructions. **Implementation Details:** | Property | Value | |----------|-------| | `id` | `"npm-release"` | | `name` | `"NPM Release"` | | `priority` | `10` | | Title | `"📦 NPM Package"` | **Required Context:** - `packageVersion` - Must be set in `CIContext`. If missing, `collect()` returns `null`. **Output Example:** ```markdown 📦 NPM Package `@cloudflare/kumo@1.2.3-beta.abc123` has been published to the npm registry. **Installation:** ```bash pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo@1.2.3-beta.abc123 ``` **Testing:** You can now test this beta version in your projects before the final release. ``` **Sources:** [ci/reporters/npm-release.ts:1-37]() ### kumoDocsPreviewReporter The `kumoDocsPreviewReporter` generates a report when documentation is deployed to a preview URL. It displays the preview URL and commit SHA. **Implementation Details:** | Property | Value | |----------|-------| | `id` | `"kumo-docs-preview"` | | `name` | `"Kumo Docs Preview"` | | `priority` | `30` | | Title | `"📚 Documentation Preview"` | **Required Context:** - `kumoDocsPreviewUrl` - Must be set in `CIContext`. If missing, `collect()` returns `null`. **Output Example:** ```markdown 📚 Documentation Preview **Preview URL:** [https://docs.kumo-ui.com/abc12345](https://docs.kumo-ui.com/abc12345) This preview deployment (`abc12345`) contains the latest documentation changes from this MR. ``` **Sources:** [ci/reporters/kumo-docs-preview.ts:1-32]() --- ## Priority Ordering Report items are sorted by their `priority` field before being formatted into markdown. This ensures consistent ordering regardless of which CI jobs complete first. **Priority Ranges:** | Range | Purpose | Example Reporters | |-------|---------|-------------------| | 10-19 | Release information | `npmReleaseReporter` (priority: 10) | | 20-29 | Reserved | - | | 30-39 | Preview deployments | `kumoDocsPreviewReporter` (priority: 30) | Lower priority numbers appear first in the final PR comment. This means release information (npm packages) always appears above preview deployments (documentation). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:28-33](), [ci/reporters/npm-release.ts:29-34](), [ci/reporters/kumo-docs-preview.ts:24-30]() --- ## Extension Points To add a new reporter to the system: 1. **Create a reporter implementation** following the `Reporter` interface pattern 2. **Define the priority** in the appropriate range (10-19 for releases, 30-39 for previews) 3. **Register the reporter** in `ci/reporters/index.ts` by adding it to the `reporters` array 4. **Export the reporter** from `ci/reporters/index.ts` for external use **Example Reporter Structure:** ```typescript import type { CIContext, ReportItem, Reporter } from "./types"; export const myCustomReporter: Reporter = { id: "my-custom-report", name: "My Custom Report", async collect(context: CIContext): Promise { // Check if required context exists if (!context.someRequiredField) { return null; } // Generate report content const content = `Your markdown content here`; return { id: "my-custom-report", title: "🎯 My Custom Report", priority: 35, // Choose appropriate priority content, success: true, }; }, }; ``` The reporter will automatically be executed during artifact generation if the required context is available. No changes are needed to the aggregation logic. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-28](), [ci/reporters/npm-release.ts:1-37](), [ci/reporters/kumo-docs-preview.ts:1-32]() --- ## File System Layout The Reporter System uses a dedicated directory for artifact storage: ``` ci/ ├── reports/ # Artifact directory (gitignored) │ ├── npm-release.json # NPM release report artifact │ └── kumo-docs-preview.json # Docs preview report artifact └── reporters/ ├── types.ts # Core interfaces and utilities ├── index.ts # Reporter registry ├── npm-release.ts # NPM release reporter └── kumo-docs-preview.ts # Docs preview reporter ``` The `ci/reports/` directory is ephemeral and should be gitignored. Artifacts exist only during the CI run and are cleaned up afterward. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:18-19](), [ci/reporters/index.ts:1-29]() --- # Page: PR Comment Automation # PR Comment Automation

## Purpose and Scope This document describes the PR comment automation system, which aggregates results from multiple parallel CI jobs into a single consolidated comment posted to GitHub pull requests. The system uses a file-based artifact pattern where individual CI jobs write report artifacts that are later collected and formatted into a markdown comment. For information about specific reporters that generate these artifacts, see [CI Script Reference](#4.3). For details about the underlying GitHub API utilities, see [CI Utilities](#4.4). For the overall reporter architecture, see [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1). **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:1-7](), [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:1-19]() ## System Architecture The PR comment automation system operates in two phases: **artifact generation** and **artifact aggregation**. Multiple CI jobs run in parallel, each potentially producing a report artifact. A final job collects all artifacts and posts a consolidated comment. ### High-Level Flow ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Phase 1: Artifact Generation" Job1["CI Job: Beta Release
(write-npm-report.ts)"] Job2["CI Job: Docs Preview
(write-kumo-docs-report.ts)"] Job3["CI Job: Custom Reporter"] Job1 --> Artifact1["npm-release.json"] Job2 --> Artifact2["kumo-docs-preview.json"] Job3 --> Artifact3["custom-report.json"] Artifact1 --> ArtifactsDir["ci/reports/"] Artifact2 --> ArtifactsDir Artifact3 --> ArtifactsDir end subgraph "Phase 2: Aggregation" ArtifactsDir --> ReadFn["readReportArtifacts()"] ReadFn --> Items["ReportItem[]"] Items --> SortFn["Sort by priority"] SortFn --> BuildFn["buildMarkdownComment()"] BuildFn --> Markdown["Markdown Comment"] Markdown --> PostFn["postPRComment()"] PostFn --> GitHub["GitHub API
POST /repos/.../issues/.../comments"] end GitHub --> PRComment["PR Comment
with consolidated report"] ``` **Diagram: Artifact-based PR Comment Flow** The system uses the filesystem as a communication channel. Each CI job writes a JSON file to the `ci/reports/` directory using `writeReportArtifact()`. The final job reads all JSON files with `readReportArtifacts()`, sorts them by priority, builds a markdown comment with `buildMarkdownComment()`, and posts it via `postPRComment()`. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:18-143](), [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:24-64](), [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:1-60]() ## Core Data Structures ### ReportItem Interface The `ReportItem` interface defines the structure of each section in the PR comment: ```mermaid classDiagram class ReportItem { +string id +string title +number priority +string content +boolean success } class CIContext { +string commitSha +string shortSha +string prNumber +string repository +string apiToken +string packageName +string packageVersion +string? kumoDocsPreviewUrl } class Reporter { +string id +string name +collect(context: CIContext) Promise~ReportItem | null~ } Reporter ..> CIContext : uses Reporter ..> ReportItem : produces ``` **Diagram: Core Type Definitions** **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:24-78]() #### ReportItem Fields | Field | Type | Purpose | |-------|------|---------| | `id` | `string` | Unique identifier matching the artifact filename (e.g., `"npm-release"`) | | `title` | `string` | Section heading displayed in the comment (e.g., `"NPM Beta Release"`) | | `priority` | `number` | Sort order; lower numbers appear first (10-19: releases, 20-29: previews) | | `content` | `string` | Markdown content for this section | | `success` | `boolean` | Whether the operation succeeded | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:24-39]() #### CIContext Fields The `CIContext` interface provides environment data to reporters: | Field | Source Environment Variable | Purpose | |-------|----------------------------|---------| | `commitSha` | `GITHUB_SHA` | Full commit SHA | | `shortSha` | Derived from `GITHUB_SHA` | First 8 characters of commit SHA | | `prNumber` | `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` or `PR_NUMBER` | Pull request number | | `repository` | `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` | Repository name (owner/repo) | | `apiToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub API authentication token | | `packageName` | `PACKAGE_NAME` | Package name being released | | `packageVersion` | `PACKAGE_VERSION` | Package version being released | | `kumoDocsPreviewUrl` | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` | Documentation preview URL (optional) | **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:44-63](), [ci/reporters/types.ts:84-96]() ## Artifact Generation Phase Individual CI jobs generate report artifacts by calling `writeReportArtifact()`: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Job as "CI Job" participant Fn as "writeReportArtifact()" participant FS as "File System" Job->>Fn: Call with ReportItem Fn->>FS: Check if ci/reports/ exists alt Directory missing Fn->>FS: mkdirSync("ci/reports/", {recursive: true}) end Fn->>FS: writeFileSync("ci/reports/{id}.json", JSON) Fn->>Job: Log "Report artifact written: ci/reports/{id}.json" ``` **Diagram: Artifact Generation Sequence** **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:98-109]() ### Artifact Directory Structure The `REPORTS_DIR` constant defines the artifact location: ``` ci/ └── reports/ ├── npm-release.json ├── kumo-docs-preview.json └── {reporter-id}.json ``` Each artifact is a JSON file named after the reporter's `id` field. The directory is created automatically if it doesn't exist. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:18-19](), [ci/reporters/types.ts:102-105]() ## Artifact Aggregation Phase The `post-pr-report.ts` script orchestrates the aggregation phase: ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["post-pr-report.ts

and item.id"] LogItems --> BuildMD["buildMarkdownComment(items, failures)"] BuildMD --> Post["postPRComment(context, comment)"] Post --> Success["Log 'PR report posted successfully'"] ``` **Diagram: Aggregation Script Flow** **Sources:** [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:24-64]() ### Reading Artifacts The `readReportArtifacts()` function implements the collection logic: ```mermaid flowchart LR Start["readReportArtifacts()"] --> CheckDir{"ci/reports/
exists?"} CheckDir -->|No| EmptyResult["{items: [], failures: []}"] CheckDir -->|Yes| ListFiles["readdirSync(REPORTS_DIR)
.filter(f => f.endsWith('.json'))"] ListFiles --> Loop["For each JSON file"] Loop --> TryRead["Try readFileSync() + JSON.parse()"] TryRead --> Success["Add to items[]"] TryRead --> Error["Add filename to failures[]"] Success --> Return["Return {items, failures}"] Error --> Return ``` **Diagram: Artifact Reading Logic** The function returns a `ReadReportResult` containing successfully parsed items and a list of files that failed to parse. Failures are logged but don't prevent the comment from being posted. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:111-143]() ## Comment Construction The `buildMarkdownComment()` function transforms report items into a formatted markdown comment: ```mermaid flowchart TB Input["buildMarkdownComment(items, failures)"] --> Sort["Sort items by priority
(ascending)"] Sort --> MapSections["Map each item to:
'### {title}\n\n{content}'"] MapSections --> CheckFail{"failures.length
> 0?"} CheckFail -->|Yes| AddWarn["Add warning section:
'Failed to load N artifacts'"] CheckFail -->|No| SkipWarn["Skip warning section"] AddWarn --> Combine["Combine sections"] SkipWarn --> Combine Combine --> AddHeader["Prepend header:
'## PR Release Summary'"] AddHeader --> AddFooter["Append footer:
'Auto-generated by Kumo CI'"] AddFooter --> Output["Return markdown string"] ``` **Diagram: Markdown Comment Assembly** **Sources:** [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:10-36]() ### Priority-Based Ordering Report items are sorted by their `priority` field to ensure consistent ordering in the final comment: | Priority Range | Report Type | Example | |----------------|-------------|---------| | 10-19 | Release information | NPM beta release status | | 20-29 | Preview deployments | Kumo docs preview URL | Lower priority numbers appear first in the comment. This ensures release information is displayed prominently at the top. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:29-33](), [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:18]() ### Comment Structure The final markdown comment follows this structure: ``` ## PR Release Summary ### {First Section Title (lowest priority number)} {First section content} ### {Second Section Title} {Second section content} ### Warning Failed to load N report artifact(s): file1.json, file2.json --- *Auto-generated by [Kumo CI](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo)* ``` **Sources:** [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:20-35]() ## Posting to GitHub The `postPRComment()` function handles the GitHub API interaction: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Script as "post-pr-report.ts" participant PostFn as "postPRComment()" participant Validate as "Validation" participant API as "postGitHubPRComment()" participant GitHub as "GitHub API" Script->>PostFn: Call with context, body PostFn->>Validate: Check prNumber and apiToken alt Missing variables Validate->>PostFn: Log missing variables PostFn->>Script: Return early else All present PostFn->>API: Call with apiToken, prNumber, body API->>GitHub: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pr}/comments GitHub->>API: 201 Created API->>PostFn: Success PostFn->>Script: Log "Posted PR comment to #{prNumber}" end ``` **Diagram: GitHub Comment Posting Sequence** The function validates that required environment variables (`prNumber` and `apiToken`) are present before attempting to post. If validation fails, it logs the missing variables and returns early without error. **Sources:** [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:38-59]() ## Error Handling The system includes multiple error handling layers: ### Artifact Parsing Failures When `readReportArtifacts()` encounters a malformed JSON file: 1. The error is caught and logged with `console.warn()` 2. The filename is added to the `failures` array 3. Processing continues for remaining artifacts 4. Failures are displayed in a "Warning" section in the final comment **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:132-140]() ### Missing Context Variables When required environment variables are missing: 1. `buildContextFromEnv()` returns default/empty values 2. `postPRComment()` validates required fields 3. Missing fields are logged but don't throw errors 4. The script exits gracefully without posting **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:84-96](), [ci/utils/pr-reporter.ts:47-54]() ### Script Execution Failures The main script wraps execution in a try-catch block: ```typescript main().catch((error) => { console.error("Failed to post PR report:", error); process.exit(1); }); ``` Any unhandled errors during aggregation or posting result in a non-zero exit code, causing the CI job to fail. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:61-64]() ## Usage in CI Workflows ### Environment Variables Required The aggregation script requires these environment variables: - `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` or `PR_NUMBER` - Pull request number - `GITHUB_TOKEN` - GitHub API authentication token - `GITHUB_SHA` - Commit SHA (for context) - `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` - Repository name (defaults to `cloudflare/kumo`) **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:84-96](), [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:14-16]() ### Execution Order The script must run **after** all jobs that produce report artifacts: ```mermaid gantt title CI Job Execution Timeline dateFormat X axisFormat %s section Parallel Jobs Beta Release Job :a1, 0, 30s Docs Preview Job :a2, 0, 45s Custom Reporter Job :a3, 0, 20s section Aggregation post-pr-report.ts :milestone, m1, 45, 0s GitHub Comment Posted :milestone, m2, 47, 0s ``` **Diagram: CI Job Timing Requirements** The aggregation job should be configured to depend on all upstream jobs, ensuring all artifacts are written before collection begins. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:8-10]() ## Extensibility ### Adding New Reporters To add a new reporter to the system: 1. Create a script that builds a `ReportItem` object 2. Call `writeReportArtifact(item)` to save the artifact 3. Use a unique `id` for the reporter (becomes the filename) 4. Set an appropriate `priority` (10-19 for releases, 20-29 for previews) 5. Ensure the script runs before `post-pr-report.ts` No changes to `post-pr-report.ts` are needed - it automatically discovers all `.json` files in the artifacts directory. **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:99-109](), [ci/scripts/post-pr-report.ts:34-41]() ### Example Reporter Implementation ```typescript import { writeReportArtifact, buildContextFromEnv } from "../reporters"; const context = buildContextFromEnv(); const item = { id: "custom-check", title: "Custom Check Results", priority: 25, content: "✅ All custom checks passed", success: true, }; writeReportArtifact(item); ``` **Sources:** [ci/reporters/types.ts:24-109]() --- # Page: CI Script Reference # CI Script Reference
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts](ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts) - [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts](ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts) - [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts](ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts)
This page provides reference documentation for individual CI scripts in the `ci/scripts/` directory. These scripts are executable TypeScript programs that perform specific tasks within the CI/CD pipeline, such as validating changesets and writing report artifacts. For information about the reporter framework and artifact aggregation, see [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1). For information about how reports are posted to PRs, see [PR Comment Automation](#4.2). For shared utility functions used by these scripts, see [CI Utilities](#4.4). ## Script Overview The CI scripts fall into two categories: **validation scripts** that enforce repository policies, and **report writer scripts** that generate artifacts for the reporter system. | Script | Type | Purpose | Called By | |--------|------|---------|-----------| | `validate-kumo-changeset.ts` | Validation | Ensures changeset exists when kumo package is modified | Git pre-push hook, CI validation workflow | | `write-kumo-docs-report.ts` | Report Writer | Generates artifact for docs preview deployment | `deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh` | | `write-npm-report.ts` | Report Writer | Generates artifact for npm beta release | `publish-beta.sh` | All scripts are executable via the `tsx` runtime and include a shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env tsx`) for direct execution. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:1-232](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:1-42](), [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:1-42]() ## Script Execution Workflow ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Validation Context" GitPush["Git Push"] --> PrePushHook["Lefthook Pre-push Hook"] PrePushHook --> ValidateCS["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] CIPRJob["CI PR Job"] --> ValidateCS end subgraph "Beta Release Context" BetaDeploy["Beta Deployment"] --> PublishBeta["publish-beta.sh"] PublishBeta --> VerifyNPM["Verify npm Publication"] VerifyNPM --> WriteNPM["write-npm-report.ts"] WriteNPM --> NPMArtifact["ci/reports/npm-release.json"] end subgraph "Preview Deployment Context" PRCreate["PR Created/Updated"] --> DeployPreview["deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh"] DeployPreview --> WranglerUpload["wrangler versions upload"] WranglerUpload --> WriteKumo["write-kumo-docs-report.ts"] WriteKumo --> KumoArtifact["ci/reports/kumo-docs-preview.json"] end subgraph "Aggregation" NPMArtifact --> PostReport["post-pr-report.ts"] KumoArtifact --> PostReport PostReport --> PRComment["PR Comment"] end ValidateCS -->|exit 1 on failure| BlockPush["Block Push/Fail CI"] ``` **Diagram: Script Execution Flow** This diagram shows how scripts are invoked within different contexts. Validation scripts run synchronously and block operations on failure, while report writers run asynchronously after deployments and write artifacts for later aggregation. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:27-126](), [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:20-36](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:20-36]() ## Validation Scripts ### validate-kumo-changeset.ts **Purpose:** Enforces that a changeset file targeting `@cloudflare/kumo` exists when files in `packages/kumo/` are modified within a pull request context. **Execution Contexts:** - Git pre-push hook (via Lefthook) - CI pull request validation workflow **Algorithm Overview:** ```mermaid graph TB Start["Script Start"] --> CheckContext["isPullRequestContext() || isLocalContext()"] CheckContext -->|false| Skip["Skip Validation"] CheckContext -->|true| CheckChanges["hasChangesInPath('packages/kumo')"] CheckChanges -->|false| SkipNoChanges["Skip: No kumo changes"] CheckChanges -->|true| GetNewCS["getNewlyAddedChangesets()"] GetNewCS --> FilterKumo["Filter changesets targeting '@cloudflare/kumo'"] FilterKumo --> CheckCount{">= 1 changeset?"} CheckCount -->|yes| Success["✅ Exit 0: Validation passed"] CheckCount -->|no| CheckAnyCS{">= 1 changeset
for any package?"} CheckAnyCS -->|yes| ErrorWrongPkg["❌ Error: Changeset exists but doesn't target kumo"] CheckAnyCS -->|no| ErrorNone["❌ Error: No changesets found"] ErrorWrongPkg --> Exit1["Exit 1"] ErrorNone --> Exit1 ``` **Diagram: Changeset Validation Logic Flow** **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:27-126]() #### Context Detection The script uses two detection mechanisms: 1. **Pull Request Context:** Detected via `isPullRequestContext()` from `git-operations.ts`, which checks for GitHub Actions environment variables (`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF`) 2. **Local Context:** Detected by absence of `CI` environment variable via `isLocalContext()` [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:31-42]() #### Change Detection The script checks for modifications in `packages/kumo/` using `hasChangesInPath()`: ```typescript const KUMO_PATH = "packages/kumo"; function checkForKumoChanges(): boolean { const result = hasChangesInPath(KUMO_PATH); if (result === null) { console.warn("⚠️ Warning: Could not determine if kumo changes exist, assuming they do"); return true; } return result; } ``` If change detection fails (returns `null`), the script conservatively assumes changes exist to avoid false negatives. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:128-139]() #### Changeset Discovery The script uses `getNewlyAddedFiles()` to find changeset files that were added in the current PR: [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:141-192]() Key behavior: - Only processes files with status `A` (Added) in `.changeset/` directory - Ignores `config.json`, `README.md`, `USAGE.md` - Parses YAML frontmatter to extract package declarations #### Changeset Parsing Changesets use YAML frontmatter to declare target packages: ```yaml --- "@cloudflare/kumo": patch --- Description of changes... ``` The parser extracts package names from lines matching the pattern `"@package/name": patch|minor|major`: [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:194-220]() #### Error Messages When validation fails, the script provides actionable guidance: ``` ❌ CHANGESET VALIDATION FAILED ❌ ERROR: Changes detected in packages/kumo/ but no NEW changeset files found 📋 To fix this issue: 1. Run: pnpm changeset 2. Select "@cloudflare/kumo" when prompted 3. Choose the appropriate change type (patch/minor/major) 4. Write a clear description of your changes 5. Commit the generated changeset file ``` In CI environments, errors are wrapped in collapsible sections using ANSI escape codes for better visibility. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:66-114]() #### Exit Codes | Exit Code | Meaning | |-----------|---------| | 0 | Validation passed or skipped (no kumo changes) | | 1 | Validation failed (kumo changes without changeset) | **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:115-126]() ## Report Writer Scripts Report writer scripts generate JSON artifacts that conform to the `ReportItem` interface defined in the reporter system. These artifacts are consumed by `post-pr-report.ts` to create consolidated PR comments. ### Common Pattern Both report writers follow the same execution pattern: ```mermaid graph LR Start["Script Start"] --> BuildCtx["buildContextFromEnv()"] BuildCtx --> ValidateEnv{"Required env vars
present?"} ValidateEnv -->|no| Error["console.error()
exit 1"] ValidateEnv -->|yes| Collect["reporter.collect(context)"] Collect --> CheckItem{"Item generated?"} CheckItem -->|yes| Write["writeReportArtifact(item)"] CheckItem -->|no| Info["Log 'No report item'"] Write --> Success["✅ Exit 0"] Info --> Success ``` **Diagram: Report Writer Script Pattern** **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:20-36](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:20-36]() ### write-npm-report.ts **Purpose:** Generates a report artifact for npm beta releases, called after `publish-beta.sh` successfully publishes the package. #### Required Environment Variables | Variable | Description | Example | |----------|-------------|---------| | `PACKAGE_VERSION` | Published package version | `0.1.0-beta.abc1234` | | `PACKAGE_NAME` | Package name (optional) | `@cloudflare/kumo` | #### Execution Flow 1. Build context from environment via `buildContextFromEnv()` 2. Validate `PACKAGE_VERSION` is present 3. Call `npmReleaseReporter.collect(context)` to generate report item 4. Write artifact via `writeReportArtifact(item)` to `ci/reports/npm-release.json` [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:20-36]() #### Output Artifact Structure The generated artifact contains: - Reporter ID: `"npm-release"` - Package version and name - npm registry URL - Emoji: 📦 - Priority: Configured in reporter definition See [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1) for complete `ReportItem` interface details. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:1-42]() ### write-kumo-docs-report.ts **Purpose:** Generates a report artifact for kumo-docs preview deployments, called after `deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh` successfully deploys to Cloudflare Workers. #### Required Environment Variables | Variable | Description | Example | |----------|-------------|---------| | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` | Deployed preview URL | `https://abc1234.kumo-ui-docs.pages.dev` | | `GITHUB_SHA` | Commit SHA (GitHub Actions) | `abc1234567890...` | #### Execution Flow 1. Build context from environment via `buildContextFromEnv()` 2. Validate `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` is present 3. Call `kumoDocsPreviewReporter.collect(context)` to generate report item 4. Write artifact via `writeReportArtifact(item)` to `ci/reports/kumo-docs-preview.json` [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:20-36]() #### Output Artifact Structure The generated artifact contains: - Reporter ID: `"kumo-docs-preview"` - Preview URL with link - Commit SHA - Emoji: 📚 - Priority: Configured in reporter definition **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:1-42]() ## Script Data Flow ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Environment Sources" GHActions["GitHub Actions
Environment Variables"] ShellScript["Shell Script

utilities"] GitOps --> ValidateCS["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] end subgraph "Script Processing" BuildCtx --> WriteNPM["write-npm-report.ts"] BuildCtx --> WriteKumo["write-kumo-docs-report.ts"] WriteNPM --> NPMReporter["npmReleaseReporter.collect()"] WriteKumo --> KumoReporter["kumoDocsPreviewReporter.collect()"] NPMReporter --> NPMItem["ReportItem"] KumoReporter --> KumoItem["ReportItem"] end subgraph "Artifact Output" NPMItem --> WriteNPMArt["writeReportArtifact()"] KumoItem --> WriteKumoArt["writeReportArtifact()"] WriteNPMArt --> NPMFile["ci/reports/

Result"] ``` **Diagram: Data Flow Through CI Scripts** This diagram shows how data flows from environment sources through context building, script processing, artifact generation, and finally to PR comments. Validation scripts bypass artifact generation and directly affect execution flow. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:14-36](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:14-36](), [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:5-10]() ## Environment Variables Reference ### Common Variables These variables are available in all CI contexts via GitHub Actions: | Variable | Source | Used By | |----------|--------|---------| | `CI` | GitHub Actions | Context detection in all scripts | | `GITHUB_SHA` | GitHub Actions | Report writers for commit identification | | `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` | GitHub Actions | `validate-kumo-changeset.ts` context detection | | `GITHUB_BASE_REF` | GitHub Actions | `validate-kumo-changeset.ts` context detection | ### Script-Specific Variables #### validate-kumo-changeset.ts No script-specific environment variables required. Relies on Git state and GitHub Actions environment. #### write-npm-report.ts | Variable | Required | Default | Description | |----------|----------|---------|-------------| | `PACKAGE_VERSION` | Yes | - | Published package version from `publish-beta.sh` | | `PACKAGE_NAME` | No | `@cloudflare/kumo` | Package name for npm registry URL | #### write-kumo-docs-report.ts | Variable | Required | Default | Description | |----------|----------|---------|-------------| | `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` | Yes | - | Preview URL from `deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh` | **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:31-42](), [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:8-26](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:8-26]() ## Error Handling ### Validation Scripts Validation scripts use exit codes to signal success or failure: - **Exit 0:** Validation passed or skipped (no relevant changes) - **Exit 1:** Validation failed with actionable error message Errors include formatted guidance for developers to resolve issues. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:115]() ### Report Writer Scripts Report writer scripts handle errors via: 1. **Environment Variable Validation:** Exit with code 1 if required variables are missing 2. **Exception Handling:** Top-level `.catch()` logs errors and exits with code 1 3. **Silent Success:** If reporter returns `null`, log informational message and exit 0 [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:23-41](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:23-41]() ## Integration Points ### With Reporter System Report writer scripts integrate with the reporter system defined in `ci/reporters/`: - Import `buildContextFromEnv()` to construct `ReporterContext` - Import specific reporter instances (`npmReleaseReporter`, `kumoDocsPreviewReporter`) - Import `writeReportArtifact()` to persist `ReportItem` objects as JSON See [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1) for complete reporter interface details. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:14-18](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:14-18]() ### With Git Operations The validation script integrates with `git-operations.ts` utilities: - `isPullRequestContext()` - Detects GitHub Actions PR context - `hasChangesInPath(path)` - Checks if files in path were modified - `getNewlyAddedFiles(dir, options)` - Lists newly added files in directory See [CI Utilities](#4.4) for complete Git operations reference. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:5-10]() ### With Shell Scripts Report writers are invoked by shell scripts after successful operations: - `publish-beta.sh` → `write-npm-report.ts` with `PACKAGE_VERSION` set - `deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh` → `write-kumo-docs-report.ts` with `KUMO_DOCS_PREVIEW_URL` set See [Beta Release Process](#5.1) and [Documentation Preview Deployments](#6.1) for shell script details. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/write-npm-report.ts:1-12](), [ci/scripts/write-kumo-docs-report.ts:1-12]() --- # Page: CI Utilities # CI Utilities

These utilities provide abstractions for common operations including Git ref resolution, file change detection, and GitHub API interactions. For information about the CI scripts that use these utilities, see [CI Script Reference](#4.3). For the reporter system architecture, see [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1). For PR comment aggregation, see [PR Comment Automation](#4.2). ## Overview The CI utilities layer provides two primary modules: | Module | Purpose | Key Functions | |--------|---------|---------------| | `git-operations.ts` | Git repository operations | `getGitRefs()`, `getChangedFiles()`, `isPullRequestContext()` | | `github-api.ts` | GitHub API interactions | `createPullRequest()`, `postPRComment()` | These utilities handle the complexity of different execution contexts (GitHub Actions vs. local development, PR vs. push events) and provide a consistent interface for CI scripts. **Sources:** [ci/utils/git-operations.ts:1-235](), [ci/utils/github-api.ts:1-65]() ## Utility Architecture The following diagram shows how CI utilities relate to scripts and external systems: ```mermaid graph TB subgraph Scripts["CI Scripts"] PostReport["post-pr-report.ts"] ValidateCS["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] CreatePR["create-release-pr.ts"] WriteReports["write-*-report.ts"] end subgraph Utilities["Utility Modules"] GitOps["git-operations.ts"] GitHubAPI["github-api.ts"] end subgraph Functions["Key Functions"] GetRefs["getGitRefs()"] GetChanged["getChangedFiles()"] IsPR["isPullRequestContext()"] GetNewFiles["getNewlyAddedFiles()"] CreatePRFunc["createPullRequest()"] PostComment["postPRComment()"] end subgraph External["External Systems"] GitCLI["Git CLI
execSync/execFileSync"] OctokitLib["@octokit/rest"] GitHubAPIExt["GitHub API"] end PostReport --> GitOps PostReport --> GitHubAPI ValidateCS --> GitOps CreatePR --> GitHubAPI WriteReports --> GitOps GitOps --> GetRefs GitOps --> GetChanged GitOps --> IsPR GitOps --> GetNewFiles GitHubAPI --> CreatePRFunc GitHubAPI --> PostComment GetRefs --> GitCLI GetChanged --> GitCLI GetNewFiles --> GitCLI CreatePRFunc --> OctokitLib PostComment --> OctokitLib OctokitLib --> GitHubAPIExt ``` **Sources:** [ci/utils/git-operations.ts:1-235](), [ci/utils/github-api.ts:1-65]() ## Git Operations Module The `git-operations.ts` module provides utilities for working with Git refs, detecting file changes, and identifying execution context. It handles differences between GitHub Actions and local development environments. ### Git Ref Resolution The `getGitRefs()` function determines the base and head refs for comparing changes, with fallback logic for different contexts: ```mermaid graph TB Start["getGitRefs()"] --> CheckBase{"GITHUB_BASE_REF
exists?"} CheckBase -->|Yes| FetchBase["Fetch origin/baseRef"] CheckBase -->|No| CheckCI{"CI environment?"} FetchBase -->|Success| ReturnOrigin["Return:

This is essential for shallow clones used in GitHub Actions. **Sources:** [ci/utils/git-operations.ts:88-128]() #### `hasChangesInPath(path, options?)` Convenience function that checks if any files changed in a specific directory: ```typescript // Usage example from CI scripts const kumoChanged = hasChangesInPath("packages/kumo"); if (kumoChanged) { // Run kumo-specific validation } ``` | Parameter | Type | Description | |-----------|------|-------------| | `path` | `string` | Directory to check | | **Returns** | `boolean \| null` | `true` if changes exist, `false` if none, `null` if unable to determine | **Sources:** [ci/utils/git-operations.ts:134-145]() #### `getNewlyAddedFiles(directory, options?)` Returns files with their git status (Added, Modified, Deleted): ```typescript interface FileWithStatus { status: string; // "A" = Added, "M" = Modified, "D" = Deleted path: string; } ``` Uses `execFileSync()` with array arguments to prevent command injection. The function filters results to a specific directory using git's `--` separator. **Sources:** [ci/utils/git-operations.ts:151-197]() ### Pull Request Context Detection The `isPullRequestContext()` function determines if the script is running in a PR context: ```mermaid graph LR Check1{"GITHUB_EVENT_NAME
== 'pull_request'?"} -->|Yes| ReturnTrue["return true"] Check1 -->|No| Check2{"GITHUB_EVENT_NAME

## Purpose and Scope This document provides an overview of the release management system for the Kumo monorepo, focusing on versioning strategies, the changeset workflow, and the relationship between beta and production releases. Release management in Kumo is built around the [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) library and enforces strict validation to ensure version control integrity. For detailed step-by-step guides, see: - **Beta releases**: [Beta Release Process](#5.1) - **Production releases**: [Production Release Process](#5.2) - **Creating and managing changesets**: [Changeset Workflow](#5.3) For CI/CD infrastructure that supports releases, see [CI/CD System](#4). ## Release Management Architecture The Kumo release system consists of three interconnected layers: changeset management, validation enforcement, and automated publishing. Changesets serve as the source of truth for version bumps, validation ensures no release occurs without proper documentation, and publishing scripts automate the npm distribution process. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Developer Layer" Dev["Developer

Each changeset is a markdown file in the `.changeset/` directory containing: 1. **Package declarations**: Which packages should be versioned 2. **Version bump type**: `patch`, `minor`, or `major` 3. **Description**: Human-readable explanation of changes ### Changeset File Structure ```yaml --- "@cloudflare/kumo": minor --- Add new Dialog component with accessibility features ``` ### When Changesets Are Required Changes to `packages/kumo/` **require** a changeset targeting `@cloudflare/kumo`. This rule is enforced by: 1. **Git pre-push hook** - Validates locally before pushing ([lefthook.yml]()) 2. **CI validation** - Runs on all pull requests ([validate-kumo-changeset.ts]()) 3. **PR reporter** - Displays validation status in PR comments **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:720-762](), [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:1-233]() ## Release Types ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Beta Releases" B1["Automated on PR Merge"] B2["Version: {version}-beta.{hash}"] B3["Tag: beta"] B4["Purpose: Testing"] end subgraph "Production Releases" P1["Manual Trigger"] P2["Version: Semantic"] P3["Tag: latest"] P4["Purpose: Stable Distribution"] end B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 B4 -.->|"After validation"| P1 ``` ### Beta Releases - **Trigger**: Automatic on merge to `main` branch - **Versioning**: Appends `-beta.{commit-hash}` suffix - **Distribution**: Published to npm with `beta` tag - **Purpose**: Enable PR reviewers to test changes in real environments - **Installation**: `pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo@0.1.0-beta.a1b2c3d` See [Beta Release Process](#5.1) for detailed workflow. ### Production Releases - **Trigger**: Manual execution by maintainers - **Versioning**: Consumes changesets, applies semantic version bump - **Distribution**: Published to npm with `latest` tag - **Purpose**: Official stable releases for production use - **Workflow**: Creates release branch → Applies versions → Opens PR See [Production Release Process](#5.2) for detailed workflow. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:763-810]() ## Validation Architecture The changeset validation system prevents releases without proper documentation by implementing checks at multiple stages of the development workflow. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Detection Layer" GitDiff["git diff origin/main...HEAD"] PathCheck["hasChangesInPath()

Runs as part of CI `checks` stage - Results included in consolidated PR comment - Blocks merge if validation fails **Beta Release Integration:** - Triggered in `beta-release` stage after PR merge - Generates npm report artifact via `write-npm-report.ts` - Report posted to PR for installation instructions **Production Release Integration:** - Creates dedicated release branch - Automates PR creation via `create-release-pr.ts` - Triggers staging deployment after merge See [CI/CD System](#4) and [Reporter System Architecture](#4.1) for complete pipeline details. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:944-976]() ## Package Distribution All releases are published to the public npm registry under the `@cloudflare/kumo` package name: **Distribution Tags:** | Tag | Purpose | Installation Command | |-----|---------|---------------------| | `latest` | Stable production releases | `pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo` | | `beta` | Pre-release testing versions | `pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo@beta` | | `{version}` | Specific version pinning | `pnpm add @cloudflare/kumo@0.1.0-beta.a1b2c3d` | **Version Resolution:** - `@cloudflare/kumo` resolves to the latest production version - `@cloudflare/kumo@beta` resolves to the most recent beta version - Beta versions are never promoted to `latest` - they are separate builds **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:763-810]() --- # Page: Beta Release Process # Beta Release Process

Beta releases provide a mechanism for testing unreleased changes in consuming applications by publishing pre-release versions to npm with unique version identifiers based on Git commit hashes. This process specifically covers: - Automatic beta versioning with commit hash suffixes - npm publication workflow - Publication verification - Report artifact generation for CI feedback For the production release workflow, see [Production Release Process](#5.2). For changeset creation and validation, see [Changeset Workflow](#5.3). --- ## Overview The beta release process is an automated CI workflow that executes when changes are merged to the main branch. It produces npm packages with version identifiers in the format `{version}-beta.{commitHash}`, allowing consumers to install specific commits for testing purposes. ```mermaid graph TB Trigger["PR Merged to main"] --> VersionScript["version-beta.sh

## Purpose and Scope This document describes the production release workflow for publishing stable versions of `@cloudflare/kumo` to npm. Production releases create clean version numbers (e.g., `1.2.3`), publish to the npm registry, and automatically create pull requests to merge version updates back to the main branch. For pre-release publishing with commit hash suffixes, see [Beta Release Process](#5.1). For the underlying changeset system that manages version information, see [Changeset Workflow](#5.3). **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:1-105]() --- ## Overview Production releases are manually triggered workflows that: - Create dedicated release branches with unique identifiers - Apply clean version numbers by removing prerelease tags from changesets - Build and publish packages to the npm registry - Verify successful publication before proceeding - Automatically create pull requests to merge version updates back to main Unlike beta releases which run automatically on PR merges, production releases require manual initiation and are intended for stable, public package versions. **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:1-16]() --- ## Release Workflow The production release process follows a linear workflow from branch creation through PR automation: ```mermaid graph TB Start["Manual Trigger

**Configuration Management** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:4-7]()): Environment variables for package name, path, and dry run mode - **Branch Creation** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:15-18]()): Creates `release/kumo-{commit-hash}` branches - **Version Processing** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:20-32]()): Runs changesets and extracts version - **Build Execution** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:34-36]()): Builds the package before publishing - **Argument Parsing** ([ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:18-54]()): Validates CLI arguments for branch names, package info, and token - **Description Generation** ([ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:56-91]()): Builds formatted markdown with installation instructions and checklist - **PR Creation** ([ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:93-121]()): Delegates to `github-api.ts` utility **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:1-105](), [ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:1-122]() --- ## Release Branch Strategy Production releases use dedicated branches to isolate version updates from ongoing development: **Branch Naming Convention:** ```bash release/kumo-{short-commit-hash} ``` Example: `release/kumo-a1b2c3d` The branch name is generated at [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:16](): ```bash RELEASE_BRANCH="release/kumo-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" ``` ### Why Release Branches? | Benefit | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Isolation** | Version changes don't conflict with main branch development | | **Traceability** | Branch name includes commit hash for audit trail | | **Review Process** | PR allows manual review before merging version updates | | **Rollback Safety** | Failed releases don't affect main branch | The branch is pushed to GitHub at [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:88]() using `--no-verify` to bypass Git hooks. **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:16-18](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:87-88]() --- ## Version Application The script applies clean production versions by running the changesets version command: ```bash pnpm run version ``` This command ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:22]()): - Removes prerelease identifiers (e.g., `-beta.123` suffixes) - Updates `package.json` with clean version numbers - Generates or updates `CHANGELOG.md` with changeset descriptions - Creates git tags for the new version ### Version Extraction After applying versions, the script extracts the new version from `package.json`: ```bash NEW_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./${PACKAGE_PATH}/package.json').version") ``` This value ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:31]()) is used for: - Commit messages - PR titles - Verification checks - PR descriptions ### Change Detection The script verifies that changesets produced actual version updates at [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:24-28](): ```bash if git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "No changes detected. No changesets to release." exit 1 fi ``` If no pending changesets exist, the release process exits early to prevent empty releases. **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:20-32]() --- ## NPM Publication and Verification ### Publication Process After building the package, the script publishes to npm using: ```bash pnpm run release ``` This command ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:49]()) is defined in the package's `package.json` and typically runs `changeset publish`, which: - Publishes the package to the npm registry - Uses credentials from `NPM_TOKEN` environment variable - Creates git tags for published versions ### Verification Mechanism The script implements a two-phase verification system to ensure successful publication: 1. **Wait Period** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:55]()): Sleeps 30 seconds for npm registry propagation 2. **Version Lookup** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:58-69]()): Checks if the version exists using two methods: ```bash # Method 1: Check all versions list AVAILABLE_VERSIONS=$(pnpm view ${PACKAGE_NAME} versions --json 2>/dev/null || echo '[]') if echo "$AVAILABLE_VERSIONS" | grep -F "\"$NEW_VERSION\"" > /dev/null; then echo "Version $NEW_VERSION successfully published" fi # Method 2: Direct version lookup elif pnpm view ${PACKAGE_NAME}@${NEW_VERSION} version > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Version $NEW_VERSION successfully published via direct lookup" fi ``` If verification fails, the script displays the last 10 available versions and exits with an error code. ### Dry Run Mode Setting `DRY_RUN=true` skips publication and displays a summary: ```bash if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then echo "[DRY RUN] Would publish ${PACKAGE_NAME}@${NEW_VERSION} to production" # Show diff, no actual publishing fi ``` **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:43-70](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:72-84]() --- ## Pull Request Automation After successful publication, the script creates a PR to merge version updates back to main: ```mermaid graph LR Script["release-production.sh"] --> Invoke["npx tsx create-release-pr.ts"] Invoke --> Parse["parseArgs()
Extract CLI arguments"] Parse --> Build["buildDescription()
Generate markdown"] Build --> Create["createPullRequest()
GitHub API call"] Create --> Result["PR Created
Returns PR number & URL"] Parse --> Args["Arguments:
--source-branch
--target-branch
--package-name
--version
--token"] ``` ### Script Invocation The PR creation is triggered at [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:96-101](): ```bash npx tsx ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts \ --source-branch="$RELEASE_BRANCH" \ --target-branch="main" \ --package-name="$PACKAGE_NAME" \ --version="$NEW_VERSION" \ --token="$GITHUB_TOKEN" ``` ### PR Structure The generated PR includes: **Title Format** ([ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:104]()): ``` chore: release @cloudflare/kumo@{version} ``` **Description Template** ([ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:61-90]()): | Section | Content | |---------|---------| | **Package Info** | Package name, version, generated by pipeline | | **Changes** | Version bump and changelog updates, npm publication | | **Installation** | npm/pnpm install commands with exact version | | **Checklist** | Pre-checked items (published, bumped, changelog) + manual review | | **Metadata** | Release branch name, auto-generated footer | ### Output The script prints the created PR details at [ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:113](): ``` Pull request created: {html_url} (PR #{number}) ``` **Sources:** [ci/scripts/create-release-pr.ts:56-121](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:94-101]() --- ## Configuration ### Environment Variables The script uses three primary environment variables: | Variable | Default | Purpose | |----------|---------|---------| | `PACKAGE_NAME` | `@cloudflare/kumo` | NPM package identifier | | `PACKAGE_PATH` | `packages/kumo` | Relative path to package directory | | `DRY_RUN` | `false` | Enable dry run mode (no publishing) | | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | *(required)* | GitHub API token for PR creation | Configuration is loaded at [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:4-7](): ```bash PACKAGE_NAME="${PACKAGE_NAME:-@cloudflare/kumo}" PACKAGE_PATH="${PACKAGE_PATH:-packages/kumo}" DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-false}" ``` ### Dry Run Mode When `DRY_RUN=true`, the script: 1. Skips npm publication ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:44-47]()) 2. Skips git push operations ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:73-76]()) 3. Displays a summary with git diff stats ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:78-85]()) This mode is useful for testing the release process without side effects. **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:4-11](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:44-85]() --- ## Error Handling and Safety Checks The release script implements several safety mechanisms: ### Pre-Publication Checks | Check | Location | Behavior | |-------|----------|----------| | **Change Detection** | [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:24-28]() | Exit if no version changes | | **Build Validation** | [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:35-36]() | Build must succeed before publish | ### Post-Publication Verification The script prevents silent failures by: 1. **Waiting for Propagation** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:55]()): 30-second delay for npm CDN sync 2. **Dual Verification** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:60-63]()): Checks both version list and direct lookup 3. **Failure Display** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:65-68]()): Shows last 10 versions if verification fails 4. **Exit Codes** ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:68]()): Non-zero exit on verification failure ### Skip CI Flag Version commits include `[skip ci]` to prevent recursive CI runs: ```bash git commit -m "chore: release ${PACKAGE_NAME}@${NEW_VERSION} [skip ci]" ``` This prevents the version bump commit from triggering additional CI workflows. ### No-Verify Push Git push operations use `--no-verify` ([ci/versioning/release-production.sh:88](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:92]()) to bypass Git hooks, which would otherwise block pushes without changesets. **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:24-28](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:40](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:52-69](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:88](), [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:92]() --- ## Manual Execution While typically triggered by CI workflows, the script can be run manually: ```bash # Standard production release ./ci/versioning/release-production.sh # Dry run to preview changes DRY_RUN=true ./ci/versioning/release-production.sh # Custom package (if needed) PACKAGE_NAME="@cloudflare/other" PACKAGE_PATH="packages/other" ./ci/versioning/release-production.sh ``` Requirements for manual execution: - Clean working directory - Pending changesets in `.changeset/` directory - `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable for PR creation - npm authentication configured (`NPM_TOKEN`) **Sources:** [ci/versioning/release-production.sh:4-11]() --- # Page: Changeset Workflow # Changeset Workflow

This document covers the changeset-based version management workflow used in Kumo. It explains how to create changesets, how they are validated, and how they integrate with release processes. For details on how changesets are consumed during releases, see [Beta Release Process](#5.1) and [Production Release Process](#5.2). **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:700-802](), [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:1-233](), [lefthook.yml:1-17]() --- ## Overview Kumo uses [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) for version management. A changeset is a declaration file that describes: - Which package(s) are affected by changes - The type of change (patch, minor, or major) - A human-readable description for the changelog **Critical requirement:** Any changes to `packages/kumo/` **must** include a changeset. This requirement is enforced by both local Git hooks and CI validation. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:700-724](), [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:13-15]() --- ## Changeset File Structure Changesets are Markdown files stored in the `.changeset/` directory. Each file uses YAML frontmatter to declare package versions, followed by a description in Markdown. **Example changeset file (`.changeset/cool-foxes-jump.md`):** ```markdown --- "@cloudflare/kumo": minor --- Add new Toast component with success, error, and warning variants ``` **File naming:** Changeset files use randomly generated names (e.g., `cool-foxes-jump.md`) to avoid merge conflicts. **YAML frontmatter format:** - Package name in quotes: `"@cloudflare/kumo"` - Change type: `patch`, `minor`, or `major` - Multiple packages can be listed in a single changeset **Markdown description:** - Appears in the generated `CHANGELOG.md` - Should clearly explain what changed and why - Use present tense (e.g., "Add" not "Added") **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:194-220](), [AGENTS.md:722-736]() --- ## Creating Changesets ### Interactive Creation Process ```bash pnpm changeset ``` This command launches an interactive CLI with the following steps: **Step 1: Select packages** ``` Which packages would you like to include? ◉ @cloudflare/kumo ◯ @cloudflare/kumo-figma ``` For Kumo component library changes, select `@cloudflare/kumo`. **Step 2: Choose change type** ``` What kind of change is this for @cloudflare/kumo? ◯ patch (0.0.1) - Bug fixes, small updates ◯ minor (0.1.0) - New components, backwards-compatible features ◯ major (1.0.0) - Breaking changes, removed components ``` **Step 3: Write description** ``` Please enter a summary for this change: > Add Toast component with multiple variants ``` **Step 4: Confirm and commit** ``` Is this your desired changeset? (Y/n) ✔ Changeset added! - .changeset/cool-foxes-jump.md ``` Commit the generated file: ```bash git add .changeset/cool-foxes-jump.md git commit -m "chore: add changeset for Toast component" ``` **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:722-736]() --- ## Validation System Architecture ```mermaid graph TB Developer["Developer Makes Changes"] GitAdd["git add packages/kumo/..."] GitCommit["git commit"] GitPush["git push"] subgraph "Local Git Hook (Lefthook)" PrePush["pre-push hook triggered"] LefthookCheck{"Skip conditions?"} RunValidation["Run validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] LocalResult{"Validation passes?"} end subgraph "CI Pipeline" PRCreated["Pull Request Created"] CICheck["Changeset validation job"] CIValidation["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] CIResult{"Validation passes?"} end subgraph "Validation Logic (validate-kumo-changeset.ts)" DetectContext["isPullRequestContext() or isLocalContext()"] CheckChanges["hasChangesInPath('packages/kumo')"] GetChangesets["getNewlyAddedChangesets()"] ParsePkg["parseChangesetPackages()"] CheckKumo{"Changeset targets

The configuration is defined in [lefthook.yml:8-17](). ### Hook Configuration ```yaml pre-push: skip: - ref: main commands: validate-changeset: run: pnpm tsx ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts skip: - merge - rebase ``` **Behavior:** - Runs on every `git push` except from the `main` branch - Skips during merge and rebase operations - Executes the validation script [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts]() ### Skip Options ```bash # Skip all Lefthook hooks LEFTHOOK=0 git push # Skip only the changeset validation REDACTED git push # Use Git's native skip git push --no-verify ``` **When to skip:** - Pushing to a personal feature branch for backup - Emergency hotfixes (with team approval) - Non-kumo changes (though validation should pass automatically) ### Troubleshooting | Issue | Solution | |-------|----------| | "Lefthook not found" | Run `pnpm lefthook install` | | "origin/main not found" | Run `git fetch origin main` | | GUI clients (Tower, SourceTree) fail | Configure PATH in client settings | | Hook doesn't run | Check if `.git/hooks/pre-push` exists | **Sources:** [lefthook.yml:1-17](), [AGENTS.md:738-762]() --- ## CI Validation The validation script [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts]() runs in CI pipelines to enforce changeset requirements on pull requests. ### Pull Request Context Detection ```mermaid graph LR Start["validate-kumo-changeset.ts"] CheckContext["isPullRequestContext()"] CheckLocal["isLocalContext()"] LogContext["logPullRequestContext()"] Start --> CheckContext CheckContext -->|"true (CI)"| LogContext CheckContext -->|"false"| CheckLocal CheckLocal -->|"true (local)"| ValidateFlow["Proceed with validation"] CheckLocal -->|"false"| Skip["Skip validation"] LogContext --> ValidateFlow ``` **Context detection logic ([ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:31-43]()):** ```typescript const shouldValidate = isPullRequestContext() || isLocalContext(); remediation instructions - Lists found changesets that don't target `@cloudflare/kumo` - CI-specific collapsible sections when `process.env.CI` is set **Sources:** `packages/kumo/` have been modified: ```typescript function checkForKumoChanges(): boolean { const result = hasChangesInPath(KUMO_PATH); if (result === null) { console.warn("⚠️ Warning: Could not determine if kumo changes exist, assuming they do"); return true; } return result; } ``` **Behavior:** - Calls `hasChangesInPath()` from `git-operations.ts` - Returns `true` if changes detected - Returns `true` (fail-safe) if detection fails - Uses `git merge-base` and `git diff` under the hood **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:128-139]() ### Changeset Discovery: `getNewlyAddedChangesets()` The function [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:141-192]() finds changesets added in the current PR/branch: ```typescript function getNewlyAddedChangesets(): ChangesetFile[] { const cwd = process.cwd().includes("packages/kumo") ? "../.." : "."; const newFiles = getNewlyAddedFiles(CHANGESET_DIR, { cwd }); const changesets: ChangesetFile[] = []; for (const { status, path: filePath } of newFiles) { if (status !== "A") continue; const fileName = filePath.split("/").pop(); if (!fileName || fileName === "config.json" || fileName === "README.md" || !fileName.endsWith(".md")) { continue; } // Parse changeset file... } return changesets; } ``` **Key behaviors:** - Only considers **newly added** files (status `"A"`) - Skips configuration files (`config.json`, `README.md`, `USAGE.md`) - Filters for `.md` files only - Returns empty array if no new changesets found (not an error by itself) **Critical distinction:** This function only returns changesets **added in the current PR**, not all existing changesets. This ensures validation checks for new changeset creation, not just the presence of any changeset. **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:141-192]() ### Package Parsing: `parseChangesetPackages()` The function [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:194-220]() extracts package names from changeset YAML frontmatter: ```typescript function parseChangesetPackages(content: string): string[] { const lines = content.split("\n"); const packages: string[] = []; let inFrontmatter = false; for (const line of lines) { if (line.trim() === "---") { inFrontmatter = !inFrontmatter; continue; } if (inFrontmatter) { const match = line.match(/^["']?([^"':]+)["']?\s*:\s*(patch|minor|major)/); if (match) { packages.push(match[1]); } } } return packages; } ``` **Parsing rules:** - Tracks frontmatter boundaries with `---` markers - Uses regex to match package declarations: `"@package/name": patch|minor|major` - Handles optional quotes around package names - Returns array of package names (e.g., `["@cloudflare/kumo"]`) **Sources:** [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:194-220]() --- ## Integration with Release Workflows Changesets serve as the input for both automated beta releases and manual production releases. ### Beta Release Integration When a PR is merged: 1. **CI detects changeset:** Beta release script reads changeset files 2. **Version calculation:** Applies changeset to determine next version 3. **Beta tag applied:** Appends `-beta.{commit-hash}` to version 4. **Package published:** Published to npm with `beta` dist-tag **Example flow:** ``` Changeset: minor → 0.1.0 Beta version: 0.1.0-beta.a1b2c3d npm install: @cloudflare/kumo@0.1.0-beta.a1b2c3d ``` See [Beta Release Process](#5.1) for complete details. ### Production Release Integration For production releases: 1. **`pnpm version` consumes changesets:** - Reads all changeset files in `.changeset/` - Calculates new version by combining change types - Updates `package.json` version - Generates/updates `CHANGELOG.md` with changeset descriptions - Removes consumed changeset files 2. **`pnpm release` publishes:** - Publishes to npm with updated version - Creates Git tags See [Production Release Process](#5.2) for complete details. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:763-810]() --- ## Best Practices ### When to Create Changesets | Change Type | Create Changeset? | Reason | |-------------|-------------------|--------| | New component | ✅ Yes (minor) | Public API addition | | Component prop added | ✅ Yes (minor) | Backwards-compatible feature | | Bug fix | ✅ Yes (patch) | Affects behavior | | Documentation only | ❌ No | Doesn't affect package | | Internal refactor | ⚠️ Maybe | Only if behavior changes | | CI/build changes | ❌ No | Doesn't affect package | | Design token changes | ✅ Yes (patch/minor) | Affects styles | **General rule:** If changes affect `packages/kumo/src/`, create a changeset. Documentation-only changes in `kumo-docs-astro` don't need changesets. ### Writing Good Descriptions **Good examples:** ```markdown Add Dialog component with modal, alert, and sheet variants Fix Button hover state transition in dark mode Update Input component to support disabled state styling ``` **Bad examples:** ```markdown Fixed bug # Too vague WIP # Not descriptive Updated component # Which component? What changed? ``` **Best practices:** - Use present tense ("Add" not "Added") - Be specific about what changed - Mention component names explicitly - Include context for breaking changes - Keep descriptions concise but clear **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:722-736]() ### Common Issues and Solutions | Issue | Cause | Solution | |-------|-------|----------| | "No changeset found" | Forgot to create changeset | Run `pnpm changeset` | | "Changeset doesn't target @cloudflare/kumo" | Wrong package selected | Create new changeset, select correct package | | "Changes detected but no NEW changeset" | Changeset already exists from previous commit | Create additional changeset for new changes | | Validation passes but shouldn't | Changes outside `packages/kumo/` | No changeset needed | | Can't push despite changeset | Working directory issues | Run `git fetch origin main` | ### AI Agent Guidelines **AI agents should:** - ✅ Create changesets with `pnpm changeset` - ✅ Validate changesets exist before submitting PRs - ✅ Write clear, descriptive changeset messages **AI agents should NOT:** - ❌ Run `pnpm version` (consumes changesets) - ❌ Run `pnpm release` (publishes to npm) - ❌ Run `pnpm publish:beta` (CI-only) - ❌ Manually edit version numbers in `package.json` **Reasoning:** Versioning and publishing require human oversight and proper npm credentials. Changeset creation is safe and encouraged. **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:704-720]() --- ## Summary The changeset workflow in Kumo provides: 1. **Structured version management:** Changesets declare version bumps with clear descriptions 2. **Automated validation:** Git hooks and CI enforce changeset creation for package changes 3. **Release automation:** Changesets feed into both beta and production release processes 4. **Clear changelog:** Changeset descriptions become changelog entries **Key files:** - [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts]() - Validation logic - [lefthook.yml:8-17]() - Git hook configuration - `.changeset/` directory - Changeset storage **Related workflows:** - [Beta Release Process](#5.1) - How changesets trigger beta releases - [Production Release Process](#5.2) - How changesets are consumed for production **Sources:** [AGENTS.md:700-810](), [ci/scripts/validate-kumo-changeset.ts:1-233](), [lefthook.yml:1-17]() --- # Page: Deployment # Deployment

## Purpose and Scope This document provides an overview of the deployment infrastructure for the Kumo documentation site (`kumo-docs-astro`). It explains how the documentation is built and deployed to Cloudflare Workers in two distinct environments: preview deployments for pull requests and staging deployments for the main branch. For detailed information about specific deployment workflows: - Preview deployment mechanics: see [Documentation Preview Deployments](#6.1) - Staging deployment mechanics: see [Documentation Staging Deployments](#6.2) For information about the broader release management system: see [Release Management](#5) ## Overview The Kumo deployment system focuses exclusively on deploying the documentation site to Cloudflare Workers. Unlike the component library itself (which is published to npm), the documentation site requires web hosting infrastructure. Cloudflare Workers provides serverless hosting with two deployment strategies: 1. **Preview Deployments**: Create temporary, versioned URLs for each pull request using `wrangler versions upload` 2. **Staging Deployments**: Update the staging environment on merges to main using `wrangler deploy --env staging` Both deployment paths follow a consistent build process: compile the `@cloudflare/kumo` library, build the `kumo-docs-astro` Astro site, and upload the resulting worker bundle to Cloudflare. **Sources**: [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh:1-80](), [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-staging.sh:1-26]() ## Deployment Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Build Phase" TriggerPR["PR Created"] --> BuildLibPR["pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build"] TriggerMain["Main Branch Merge"] --> BuildLibMain["pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo build"] BuildLibPR --> BuildDocsPR["pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo-docs-astro build"] BuildLibMain --> BuildDocsMain["pnpm --filter @cloudflare/kumo-docs-astro build"] end subgraph "Deployment Phase" BuildDocsPR --> WranglerPreview["wrangler versions upload"] BuildDocsMain --> WranglerStaging["wrangler deploy --env staging"] WranglerPreview --> VersionID["Extracts Worker Version ID"] VersionID --> ConstructURL["Constructs Preview URL:
https://{version-prefix}-kumo-docs.design-engineering.workers.dev"] WranglerStaging --> StagingURL["staging.kumo-ui.com"] end subgraph "Cloudflare Workers Infrastructure" ConstructURL --> CFPreview["Cloudflare Worker
Version (Preview)"] StagingURL --> CFStaging["Cloudflare Worker

CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID"] -.->|required| WranglerPreview Auth -.->|required| WranglerStaging end ``` **Deployment Architecture** This diagram illustrates the complete deployment flow from build trigger to live worker. Both preview and staging paths begin with building the component library and documentation site in sequence. The preview path uses `wrangler versions upload` to create a versioned worker deployment, extracting the version ID from the output and constructing a preview URL. The staging path uses `wrangler deploy --env staging` to update the staging environment directly. Preview deployments integrate with the reporter system to post URLs in PR comments, while staging deployments are fire-and-forget. Both paths require Cloudflare authentication credentials as environment variables. **Sources**: [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh:20-79](), [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-staging.sh:15-25]() ## Deployment Environments The Kumo documentation site uses two distinct deployment environments with different purposes and triggers: | Environment | Trigger | Command | URL Format | Purpose | |------------|---------|---------|------------|---------| | **Preview** | Pull request creation | `wrangler versions upload` | `https://{version-prefix}-kumo-docs.design-engineering.workers.dev` | Temporary preview for code review | | **Staging** | Merge to `main` branch | `wrangler deploy --env staging` | `staging.kumo-ui.com` | Semi-permanent staging environment | ### Preview Environment Preview deployments use Cloudflare Workers' versioning system to create immutable snapshots of the documentation site. Each upload generates a unique version ID, and the first 8 characters of this ID form the `version-prefix` in the preview URL. This ensures that every PR gets a unique, stable URL that won't change even if the PR is updated. The preview environment requires the `preview_urls` flag to be enabled in both the Cloudflare dashboard (Workers & Pages > kumo-docs > Settings > Domains & Routes > Preview URLs) and in `wrangler.jsonc`. **Sources**: [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh:7-10](), [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-preview.sh:43-59]() ### Staging Environment Staging deployments use a named Wrangler environment (`staging`) configured in `wrangler.jsonc`. Unlike preview deployments, staging deploys update the same worker environment on each deployment, providing a stable URL for the latest merged changes from main. **Sources**: [ci/versioning/deploy-kumo-docs-staging.sh:21-23]() ## Build Process ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Package Dependencies" KumoLib["@cloudflare/kumo
